# Where Novis deliberately differs from PHP

Every rule carrying a `divergesFromPhp` note, with the rule that owns it. Generated from `docs/rules/` by `bun nv rules --render`.

| Topic | Divergence | Rule |
|---|---|---|
| Programs | existing PHP packages, frameworks and code do not run, and no document may imply otherwise | [`programs/no-compatibility-promise`](rules/programs.md#programs-no-compatibility-promise) |
| Programs | a plugin roster is a compile-time array literal, not a `foreach` over `new $className` | [`programs/implementing`](rules/programs.md#programs-implementing) |
| Programs | a plugin roster with its metadata is one compile-time array literal, not a `ReflectionClass` sweep over discovered classes | [`programs/implementing-with`](rules/programs.md#programs-implementing-with) |
| Programs | there is no `spl_autoload_register`, no `__autoload` and no `new $name` — a name held in a string can never reach a file | [`programs/no-runtime-autoload`](rules/programs.md#programs-no-runtime-autoload) |
| Programs | the map is a declaration in source rather than a registered loader or a `psr-4` manifest, and it travels with the code instead of with the deployment | [`programs/autoload`](rules/programs.md#programs-autoload) |
| Programs | PSR-4 imposes this by convention; here it is a diagnostic | [`programs/one-declaration-per-autoloaded-file`](rules/programs.md#programs-one-declaration-per-autoloaded-file) |
| Programs | `require` does not inherit the filesystem's case behaviour, so a path that resolves on Windows or macOS resolves on Linux or fails on all three | [`programs/path-case`](rules/programs.md#programs-path-case) |
| Programs | PHP resolves a relative `fopen` path against the process's working directory; here a literal resolves against its own source file, and nothing resolves against the working directory implicitly | [`programs/path-literals-resolve-from-their-file`](rules/programs.md#programs-path-literals-resolve-from-their-file) |
| Programs | the ORM, the service container, the facade, the route cache and the autoload dump have no equivalent, and each is absent by construction rather than by omission | [`programs/framework-refusals`](rules/programs.md#programs-framework-refusals) |
| Types | a local, a `foreach` binding, a `for` counter and a destructuring target all carry a written type, and PHP source with none does not compile | [`types/declaration`](rules/types.md#types-declaration) |
| Types | `017` is decimal seventeen where PHP reads octal fifteen; PHP's leading-zero octal is refused rather than reinterpreted | [`types/integer-literals`](rules/types.md#types-integer-literals) |
| Types | a fractional literal is not born a `float` — `decimal $price = 19.99;` is exact — and there is no literal suffix for any numeric type | [`types/numeric-literal-placement`](rules/types.md#types-numeric-literal-placement) |
| Types | PHP has one integer type; Novis has two, told apart by `Core\Reflect::typeOf` and by `$x is uint` (`rule:types/type-test`), so a value PHP's `is_int()` accepted answers `is uint` and not `is int`, and the whole 64-bit range is representable | [`types/uint`](rules/types.md#types-uint) |
| Types | `PHP_INT_MAX + 1` throws `ArithmeticError` instead of becoming a `float`, `int` against `uint` does not compile, and a `bool`, `string`, `array<T>` or object operand has no `+` at all | [`types/arithmetic`](rules/types.md#types-arithmetic) |
| Types | the widening throws above 2^53 instead of rounding, and no other implicit coercion survives | [`types/implicit-widening`](rules/types.md#types-implicit-widening) |
| Types | `bcmath` and `gmp` are retired rather than ported — exact fractional arithmetic is a register-sized scalar, and arbitrary-magnitude integers are `Core\BigInt` | [`types/decimal`](rules/types.md#types-decimal) |
| Types | there is no fallback ordering — PHP orders anything by converting an operand first, and Novis refuses a `string`, `bytes`, `array<T>`, `callable`, enum case or `null` operand where it is written | [`types/ordering`](rules/types.md#types-ordering) |
| Types | `strlen` counts bytes and needs `mb_strlen` plus a correct ambient encoding to count characters; a Novis `string` has one encoding and one length, counting extended grapheme clusters unconditionally | [`types/string-is-utf8`](rules/types.md#types-string-is-utf8) |
| Types | PHP has one type for text and for a buffer and never says which a value is; a request body, a socket read, a file's contents and a digest all arrive as `bytes` and become text only by a conversion that can throw | [`types/bytes`](rules/types.md#types-bytes) |
| Types | there is no integer key — `Core\Arr::keys()` returns `array<string>` and a `foreach` key binds as a `string` — and an element type is declared and enforced on every write, reading covariantly | [`types/arrays`](rules/types.md#types-arrays) |
| Types | there is no `merge` under any spelling and no array `+` operator; `array_merge`'s rule chosen by a key's type does not survive a language where every key is a `string` | [`types/array-combination`](rules/types.md#types-array-combination) |
| Types | PHP renumbers integer keys and silently keeps string ones; `false` means the result is a list, and nothing else | [`types/preserve-keys`](rules/types.md#types-preserve-keys) |
| Types | a read that finds no array and no key is a catchable throw, never PHP's warning and a `null` | [`types/mixed-subscript`](rules/types.md#types-mixed-subscript) |
| Types | a computed property name is not a string at the site — every other operand is refused, dispatch through a computed *method* name stays refused, and a `readonly` field in the set is refused at the write | [`types/property-key-access`](rules/types.md#types-property-key-access) |
| Types | there is no `is_int()`-style free function to narrow with — the question is the `is` operator (`rule:types/type-test`) — and `mixed` never absorbs implicitly: `int $n = $m;` is a diagnostic rather than a runtime check | [`types/unions-and-mixed`](rules/types.md#types-unions-and-mixed) |
| Types | `int` and `uint` are separate tags, so a `BIGINT UNSIGNED` value answers `is uint` and not `is int` where `is_int()` was true for both, and `string` and `bytes` are separate the same way; `is 3.14` is refused outright, there being no float literal type | [`types/type-test`](rules/types.md#types-type-test) |
| Types | nothing converts silently — `(int)"abc"` is not `0`, `PHP_INT_MAX + 1` is not a `float`, and `settype` does not exist; every conversion is written, checked, and throws rather than substituting | [`types/conversion`](rules/types.md#types-conversion) |
| Types | `(int)`, `(uint)`, `(float)`, `(string)`, `(bool)`, `(array)` and `(object)` are all parse errors rather than a second spelling of `as` | [`types/no-legacy-cast`](rules/types.md#types-no-legacy-cast) |
| Types | PHP's bare-name string, `"Class::method"` string and `[$obj, 'method']` array are all refused, and `__invoke` has no meaning — `$obj(...)` is a diagnostic whatever the class declares | [`types/callable-is-a-closure`](rules/types.md#types-callable-is-a-closure) |
| Types | `function (...) {...}` and `function (...) use (...) {...}` do not parse at all; `fn` gains the block body PHP's arrow form never had | [`types/closure-literal`](rules/types.md#types-closure-literal) |
| Types | there is no `Closure` type, no `Closure::fromCallable`, and no `call_user_func`/`call_user_func_array` | [`types/callable-absorbs-closure`](rules/types.md#types-callable-absorbs-closure) |
| Types | capture is never written, and `use (&$y)` has no replacement — a shared mutable cell is an ordinary object in user code | [`types/implicit-capture`](rules/types.md#types-implicit-capture) |
| Types | there is no shorthand `{x, y}` and no computed key, so no path leads back to PHP's dynamic properties | [`types/object-literal`](rules/types.md#types-object-literal) |
| Types | a missing name, a wrong-typed write and a receiver holding no object are all catchable throws, never a warning plus a `null`, and a write can never create a field | [`types/erased-member-access`](rules/types.md#types-erased-member-access) |
| Types | `$m::class` on a `mixed` is refused where it is written rather than failing at run time; narrow the receiver first, the way `->` already requires | [`types/class-constant`](rules/types.md#types-class-constant) |
| Expressions | the implicit conversion to `bool` is confined to six positions, where PHP applies it wherever a `bool` is wanted | [`expressions/truthy-positions`](rules/expressions.md#expressions-truthy-positions) |
| Expressions | `bytes` has no PHP neighbour and takes emptiness alone, so a one-octet `"0"` buffer is truthy where the string `"0"` is falsy | [`expressions/truthy-table`](rules/expressions.md#expressions-truthy-table) |
| Expressions | the low-precedence keyword connectives are gone entirely, and `xor` has no operator replacement at all | [`expressions/no-keyword-logical-operators`](rules/expressions.md#expressions-no-keyword-logical-operators) |
| Expressions | there is no loose-versus-strict pair to pick between — one operator, which never converts either operand | [`expressions/one-equality-operator`](rules/expressions.md#expressions-one-equality-operator) |
| Expressions | each row where PHP's two operators disagreed takes `===`'s answer — two strings compare as text and never as numbers, and an array compares in key order | [`expressions/equality-semantics`](rules/expressions.md#expressions-equality-semantics) |
| Expressions | a cross-type pairing is `false` rather than PHP's converting comparison, and it is the one place a comparison answers instead of refusing to compile | [`expressions/mixed-equality`](rules/expressions.md#expressions-mixed-equality) |
| Expressions | PHP's `==` walked properties; here there is no property walk, no `__equals`, no `equals()` protocol and no `Equatable` interface | [`expressions/object-identity-equality`](rules/expressions.md#expressions-object-identity-equality) |
| Expressions | `"1" == 1` neither answers `true` nor `false`; it does not compile, and the diagnostic names the conversion the author meant | [`expressions/disjoint-comparison-refused`](rules/expressions.md#expressions-disjoint-comparison-refused) |
| Expressions | `switch` no longer compares loosely while `match` compares identically — there is one comparison, and both use it | [`expressions/switch-match-equality`](rules/expressions.md#expressions-switch-match-equality) |
| Expressions | a malformed pattern, URI, duration or format string is a compile error at the offset inside the literal, rather than a throw on the first request that reaches the call | [`expressions/intrinsic-literals`](rules/expressions.md#expressions-intrinsic-literals) |
| Expressions | one of PHP's two destructuring spellings is refused, so `list($a, $b) = $pair;` is a diagnostic naming the bracket form | [`expressions/bracket-destructuring`](rules/expressions.md#expressions-bracket-destructuring) |
| Expressions | a failed conversion is a `null` the caller tests, where `(int)$x` — which does not parse at all — answered `0` and said nothing | [`expressions/nullable-conversion`](rules/expressions.md#expressions-nullable-conversion) |
| Expressions | there is no operator downcast: `$s as ?Core\Uri` is a compile error rather than a cast, and text reaches a class only through that class's own reader | [`expressions/nullable-conversion-availability`](rules/expressions.md#expressions-nullable-conversion-availability) |
| Expressions | no validator sits next to a parser the way `filter_var` sits next to `parse_url`; `tryParse` is `parse` with the throw caught, so the two can never read one string differently | [`expressions/try-parse`](rules/expressions.md#expressions-try-parse) |
| Expressions | PHP 8.5's `|>` applies a callable resolved at run time; this one substitutes `$_` in the parser, so the emitted tree is the nested spelling's and no closure is allocated | [`expressions/pipeline-substitution`](rules/expressions.md#expressions-pipeline-substitution) |
| Expressions | PHP has no expression-level `catch`; a one-line fallback for a throwing call is a language form rather than a swallowed `@` or a five-line block | [`expressions/catch-expression`](rules/expressions.md#expressions-catch-expression) |
| Expressions | PHP's `@` is gone, and the one-liner that would regrow it is named at compile time instead | [`expressions/bare-throwable-arm-warns`](rules/expressions.md#expressions-bare-throwable-arm-warns) |
| Statements | a file opening with `<?php` reports a diagnostic, though the code after the tag still parses | [`statements/nvs-is-the-only-open-tag`](rules/statements.md#statements-nvs-is-the-only-open-tag) |
| Statements | a relative qualified name (`Models\User` inside `namespace App;`) names nothing, and a namespace-prefix import reaches nothing under it | [`statements/a-qualified-name-is-absolute`](rules/statements.md#statements-a-qualified-name-is-absolute) |
| Statements | there is no fallback to the root namespace, so a namespaced file that catches writes `use Throwable;` | [`statements/no-fallback-to-the-root-namespace`](rules/statements.md#statements-no-fallback-to-the-root-namespace) |
| Statements | `\App\Models\User`, `use \App\Models\User;` and `namespace \App;` are each refused rather than accepted and ignored | [`statements/a-leading-separator-does-not-parse`](rules/statements.md#statements-a-leading-separator-does-not-parse) |
| Statements | `use Foo\Bar as Baz;` is a diagnostic, and no function anywhere registers a second name for a class | [`statements/nothing-gets-a-second-name`](rules/statements.md#statements-nothing-gets-a-second-name) |
| Statements | `include`, `include_once` and `require_once` are parse-time refusals — there is no warn-and-continue and no repeat guard | [`statements/require-is-the-only-inclusion-construct`](rules/statements.md#statements-require-is-the-only-inclusion-construct) |
| Statements | an included file cannot see the includer's locals, and the includer cannot see its own | [`statements/a-required-file-shares-declarations-not-locals`](rules/statements.md#statements-a-required-file-shares-declarations-not-locals) |
| Statements | `self::m()` and `parent::m()` inside a closure set the called class to the class the closure is written in, where PHP forwards the enclosing method's called class; `self::m()` in a method body on an `abstract static` `m` runs the subclass's body, where PHP throws | [`statements/static-is-a-member-modifier`](rules/statements.md#statements-static-is-a-member-modifier) |
| Statements | `static int $calls = 0;` inside a function and `global $x;` are both parse-time refusals, each naming a class static, a constant or a parameter as the replacement | [`statements/no-function-static-and-no-global`](rules/statements.md#statements-no-function-static-and-no-global) |
| Statements | there is no global constant and no superglobal, so nothing holds state without a declaration a reader can find | [`statements/storage-that-outlives-a-call`](rules/statements.md#statements-storage-that-outlives-a-call) |
| Statements | `$_SERVER`, `$_GET`, `$_POST`, `$_COOKIE`, `$_FILES`, `$_SESSION`, `$_ENV`, `$argv` and `$argc` do not exist as variables at all | [`statements/no-host-populated-variables`](rules/statements.md#statements-no-host-populated-variables) |
| Statements | neither gets a `Core` class, so `extract($_GET)`-shaped code has no straight-line conversion | [`statements/globals-and-request-are-dropped-outright`](rules/statements.md#statements-globals-and-request-are-dropped-outright) |
| Statements | a closure that never names `$this` is unbound, and `bindTo()`/`bind()` on it return an equivalent closure rather than rebinding anything | [`statements/a-closure-binds-this-only-where-it-uses-it`](rules/statements.md#statements-a-closure-binds-this-only-where-it-uses-it) |
| Statements | `&$x` is not a by-reference marker; the word is `inout` and it goes before the type | [`statements/inout-is-the-by-reference-spelling`](rules/statements.md#statements-inout-is-the-by-reference-spelling) |
| Statements | PHP removed call-time by-reference in 5.4 and left the caller no marker at all; here the marker is mandatory in both directions | [`statements/inout-is-written-at-the-call`](rules/statements.md#statements-inout-is-written-at-the-call) |
| Statements | `&` keeps only bitwise AND, logical AND and the intersection type; every by-reference spelling of it is a diagnostic | [`statements/ampersand-is-not-a-by-reference-marker`](rules/statements.md#statements-ampersand-is-not-a-by-reference-marker) |
| Statements | `die` and `die('bye')` do not compile; `exit` is the exact replacement | [`statements/exit-is-the-only-termination-keyword`](rules/statements.md#statements-exit-is-the-only-termination-keyword) |
| Classes | a global function or a global constant cannot be declared at all — every callable is a method, every constant a class constant, and there is no exception for built-ins | [`classes/no-free-functions-or-constants`](rules/classes.md#classes-no-free-functions-or-constants) |
| Classes | class, interface and method names no longer fold case, so a mis-cased reference is a diagnostic instead of a silent match | [`classes/names-resolve-case-sensitively`](rules/classes.md#classes-names-resolve-case-sensitively) |
| Classes | `IF`, `TRUE` and `NULL` are not keywords or literals — they lex as ordinary identifiers, and only `<?NVS` gets a diagnostic of its own | [`classes/reserved-spellings-are-lower-case`](rules/classes.md#classes-reserved-spellings-are-lower-case) |
| Classes | PHP's `_private` and `$_unused` conventions do not compile; there is no leading-underscore allowance in any identifier category | [`classes/no-leading-underscore-identifiers`](rules/classes.md#classes-no-leading-underscore-identifiers) |
| Classes | the constructor is spelled `constructor`; `__construct` is refused where it is written, with a diagnostic naming the rename | [`classes/constructor-is-a-method-named-constructor`](rules/classes.md#classes-constructor-is-a-method-named-constructor) |
| Classes | the mismatch is refused at the `new` rather than discovered when the wrong subclass arrives | [`classes/constructor-compatibility`](rules/classes.md#classes-constructor-compatibility) |
| Classes | a constructor that leaves a typed property unset on some path is refused at compile time rather than throwing at whichever read discovers it | [`classes/definite-property-initialization`](rules/classes.md#classes-definite-property-initialization) |
| Classes | there are no dynamic properties and no `__get`/`__set` to catch one — a wrong name is a diagnostic or a checked throw, never a newly created field | [`classes/no-dynamic-properties`](rules/classes.md#classes-no-dynamic-properties) |
| Classes | `unset($obj->prop)` does not remove a property — the one surviving operand is an array element | [`classes/unset-is-refused-on-a-property`](rules/classes.md#classes-unset-is-refused-on-a-property) |
| Classes | `__get`/`__set` are not recognized by name; observation is a declared `implements` that sees every property, not an ambient fallback that sees only the undefined ones | [`classes/property-observer`](rules/classes.md#classes-property-observer) |
| Classes | there is no `insteadof`; the only way to pick a winner is an ordinary override that calls the source it wants by name | [`classes/member-conflict-is-an-error`](rules/classes.md#classes-member-conflict-is-an-error) |
| Classes | `trait`, a class-body `use Trait;` and `insteadof` are not in the grammar at all | [`classes/no-traits`](rules/classes.md#classes-no-traits) |
| Classes | 8.4 admits a hooked property in an interface; Novis admits no property there at all | [`classes/interfaces-declare-no-state`](rules/classes.md#classes-interfaces-declare-no-state) |
| Classes | PHP's recursive property-by-property comparison of two same-class objects does not exist; ordering an unorderable pair is a compile error rather than an ambient walk | [`classes/comparable`](rules/classes.md#classes-comparable) |
| Classes | two objects of different classes are a compile error rather than a comparison PHP answers by falling through its own coercion rules | [`classes/comparable-is-same-class-only`](rules/classes.md#classes-comparable-is-same-class-only) |
| Classes | `__toString` is not recognized; the capability is `implements Stringable` and its absence is refused where the object is rendered | [`classes/stringable`](rules/classes.md#classes-stringable) |
| Classes | a double-underscore method name is refused where it is written, so no class can declare a hook the runtime would call on its own | [`classes/no-magic-methods`](rules/classes.md#classes-no-magic-methods) |
| Classes | dispatch to an undeclared method name does not exist in any form, and the two names cannot even be written down | [`classes/no-call-magic`](rules/classes.md#classes-no-call-magic) |
| Classes | `__destruct` does not exist in any form, and nothing user-declared runs when a refcount reaches zero | [`classes/no-destructors`](rules/classes.md#classes-no-destructors) |
| Classes | `__debugInfo` does not exist, so a dump cannot be filtered, renamed or synthesized by the class being dumped | [`classes/no-debug-hook`](rules/classes.md#classes-no-debug-hook) |
| Classes | `__clone`, `__serialize`, `__unserialize`, `__sleep` and `__wakeup` do not exist, so a copy always means what the language says it means | [`classes/two-copy-depths`](rules/classes.md#classes-two-copy-depths) |
| Classes | PHP's open, cross-version `serialize` wire format is not readable, and no hook fires during reconstruction, so the object-injection class has nothing to drive | [`classes/serialize-is-a-closed-format`](rules/classes.md#classes-serialize-is-a-closed-format) |
| Classes | `json_encode` reports a recursive reference by returning `false` and setting `JSON_ERROR_RECURSION`, and names no path; here the encoder throws and the message carries the property chain that closed the cycle | [`classes/an-encoder-ends-a-cycle-by-identity`](rules/classes.md#classes-an-encoder-ends-a-cycle-by-identity) |
| Classes | `class_alias` does not exist and will not be added, so no class ever answers to a second runtime-reachable name | [`classes/no-class-alias`](rules/classes.md#classes-no-class-alias) |
| Enums | every case has an integer value even where none is written, so PHP's valueless pure case does not exist | [`enums/declaration`](rules/enums.md#enums-declaration) |
| Enums | `case Hearts = 1;` is not a spelling this language has — an enum body is a comma list | [`enums/no-case-keyword`](rules/enums.md#enums-no-case-keyword) |
| Enums | an enum is not a class in disguise — a case is a compile-time constant, with no singleton, no allocation and no identity | [`enums/closed-integer-type`](rules/enums.md#enums-closed-integer-type) |
| Enums | there is no pure enum and no `string`-backed enum, and `BackedEnum` and `UnitEnum` do not exist | [`enums/one-backing-type`](rules/enums.md#enums-one-backing-type) |
| Enums | a case is a scalar, so it copies across an isolate boundary like an `int` and has no identity to preserve | [`enums/representation`](rules/enums.md#enums-representation) |
| Enums | no methods, no interfaces, no enum constants, and no `::cases()`, `::from()`, `::tryFrom()`, `->value` or `->name` | [`enums/no-class-machinery`](rules/enums.md#enums-no-class-machinery) |
| Enums | there are no case instances for a description to hand back — it carries the type's name and its case list, and nothing that acts | [`enums/reflection`](rules/enums.md#enums-reflection) |
| Iteration | an object is iterable only by declaring `Iterable<T>` or `Iterator<T>`; walking an ordinary object's public properties does not compile | [`iteration/foreach-subjects`](rules/iteration.md#iteration-foreach-subjects) |
| Iteration | no `rewind()`, `key()`, `valid()` or `IteratorAggregate`, and none of the ~20 SPL iterator classes; a cursor has two members and no key half | [`iteration/two-interfaces`](rules/iteration.md#iteration-two-interfaces) |
| Iteration | `ArrayAccess` and `Countable` do not exist; a collection exposes `->get($k)`, `->set($k, $v)` and `->count()` instead | [`iteration/no-magic-collection-interfaces`](rules/iteration.md#iteration-no-magic-collection-interfaces) |
| Iteration | reading a cursor before it has advanced, or after it is drained, is an error rather than a `null` or a stale element | [`iteration/cursor-out-of-range`](rules/iteration.md#iteration-cursor-out-of-range) |
| Iteration | a generator is a compiled state machine rather than a suspended stack, so it costs one small object and behaves the same on every compile target | [`iteration/generators`](rules/iteration.md#iteration-generators) |
| Iteration | no `yield from`, no `send()`, no `throw()` into a generator, no keyed `yield`, and no generator return value to retrieve | [`iteration/one-way-only`](rules/iteration.md#iteration-one-way-only) |
| Iteration | a helper called from a generator cannot yield into it; delegation is written as a `foreach` that re-yields | [`iteration/yield-lexical-confinement`](rules/iteration.md#iteration-yield-lexical-confinement) |
| Attributes | an attribute is never an object — PHP builds a real one the first time `ReflectionAttribute::newInstance()` is called, and needs a declared `#[Attribute]` class for every attribute kind | [`attributes/inert-metadata`](rules/attributes.md#attributes-inert-metadata) |
| Attributes | a named attribute resolves to a `type` alias rather than to a class, so there is no per-attribute-kind declaration and no second namespace of attribute names | [`attributes/attach-sites-and-forms`](rules/attributes.md#attributes-attach-sites-and-forms) |
| Attributes | PHP admits any expression as an attribute argument, `new` included, so building one has an execution order and side effects | [`attributes/payload-is-a-compile-time-constant`](rules/attributes.md#attributes-payload-is-a-compile-time-constant) |
| Attributes | repeatability is the default and needs no `Attribute::IS_REPEATABLE` marker | [`attributes/repeatable`](rules/attributes.md#attributes-repeatable) |
| Attributes | `Foo::BAR < X > ($y)` reads as a call carrying a type argument where PHP reads two comparisons | [`attributes/call-site-type-argument`](rules/attributes.md#attributes-call-site-type-argument) |
| Attributes | there is no `ReflectionAttribute` and no lookup by attribute class name; two unrelated libraries can ask for the same shape without agreeing on a name | [`attributes/structural-retrieval`](rules/attributes.md#attributes-structural-retrieval) |
| Attributes | "which one did I get?" for a repeated attribute is a diagnostic at the call site rather than a question a test run answers, and no reflection table reaches the compiled unit | [`attributes/retrieval-folds-while-checking`](rules/attributes.md#attributes-retrieval-folds-while-checking) |
| Attributes | an annotation that disagrees with the handler is a compile error rather than a documentation bug nobody notices | [`attributes/api-adds-and-cannot-contradict`](rules/attributes.md#attributes-api-adds-and-cannot-contradict) |
| Attributes | no PHP framework can refuse to build a route whose author wrote no access decision | [`attributes/access-is-a-required-sibling`](rules/attributes.md#attributes-access-is-a-required-sibling) |
| Errors | `catch (Throwable)` provably cannot see a resource-limit fatal; `Exception` and `Error` are not class names | [`errors/throwable-hierarchy`](rules/errors.md#errors-throwable-hierarchy) |
| Errors | an exception is a status value checked after every call, not a stack unwind | [`errors/propagation`](rules/errors.md#errors-propagation) |
| Errors | throwing is not a performance cliff, so exceptions may be used on ordinary control-flow paths | [`errors/throw-is-not-slower`](rules/errors.md#errors-throw-is-not-slower) |
| Errors | recursion is bounded by an 8 MB native stack rather than by `memory_limit`, so deep PHP recursion needs a rewrite | [`errors/stack-depth`](rules/errors.md#errors-stack-depth) |
| Errors | the handler is request-local rather than global, and runs on a reserve carved out before execution started | [`errors/on-limit`](rules/errors.md#errors-on-limit) |
| Errors | every failure category ends in a log line, and no handler is ever given a second attempt at the same failure | [`errors/escalation-ladder`](rules/errors.md#errors-escalation-ladder) |
| Errors | the handler is request-local and fires exactly once; there is no global `set_exception_handler` | [`errors/on-uncaught-throw`](rules/errors.md#errors-on-uncaught-throw) |
| Errors | there is one model behind every diagnostic, so a value's type is never lost the way `print_r` loses it | [`errors/diagnostic-record`](rules/errors.md#errors-diagnostic-record) |
| Errors | no stack is captured per record, where `getTrace` snapshots the whole stack at construction; the call path is the trace's answer and a record carries only where it was produced | [`errors/a-record-names-where-it-was-produced`](rules/errors.md#errors-a-record-names-where-it-was-produced) |
| Errors | a cut, a cycle and a redaction are nodes in the record, so every rendering agrees on them instead of truncating per formatter | [`errors/record-transformations`](rules/errors.md#errors-record-transformations) |
| Errors | one member replaces `var_dump`, `print_r`, `var_export` and `json_encode`, and reads correctly in every medium | [`errors/renderings`](rules/errors.md#errors-renderings) |
| Errors | no `__debugInfo` and no `__toString` in a dump — a dump shows declared state and never a prettier view of it | [`errors/no-render-hook`](rules/errors.md#errors-no-render-hook) |
| Errors | a forgotten dump writes a log line; the spelling that puts it in a production response does not exist | [`errors/debug-dump`](rules/errors.md#errors-debug-dump) |
| Errors | five levels rather than PSR-3's eight, because nobody has a rule for choosing `notice` over `info` | [`errors/log-level`](rules/errors.md#errors-log-level) |
| Errors | nothing is normalised, unfolded, mangled or truncated into an interpretation | [`errors/ambiguous-input-refused`](rules/errors.md#errors-ambiguous-input-refused) |
| Errors | the outbound half is held to the same list, with no per-call opt-out | [`errors/http-message-defects`](rules/errors.md#errors-http-message-defects) |
| Errors | no `.`-and-space mangling of cookie names, and `__Host-`/`__Secure-` are enforced by the runtime rather than by every read site | [`errors/cookie-name-bytes`](rules/errors.md#errors-cookie-name-bytes) |
| Errors | Windows device names, trailing dots and 8.3 short names are refused on Linux and macOS too | [`errors/path-component-refusals`](rules/errors.md#errors-path-component-refusals) |
| Tooling | a `#!` first line is stripped by PHP but the file still needs `<?php` on line 2; here the shebang itself opens code mode, and a `<?nvs` after it is E0009 | [`tooling/shebang-opens-code-mode`](rules/tooling.md#tooling-shebang-opens-code-mode) |
| Tooling | there is no `php -a`; the loop an interactive shell serves is `nvs run` over a cached artifact and `nvs test` | [`tooling/no-repl`](rules/tooling.md#tooling-no-repl) |
| Tooling | `Core\Ast` is built in where PHP needs `nikic/php-parser` or the PECL `ast` extension, and there is no `setAccessible(true)` | [`tooling/reflection-and-source-parsing-are-core-features`](rules/tooling.md#tooling-reflection-and-source-parsing-are-core-features) |
| Tooling | `echo` in a scheduled script, a job worker or a test neutralizes control bytes rather than writing raw, and only an HTTP request makes it HTML | [`tooling/echo-always-has-a-sink`](rules/tooling.md#tooling-echo-always-has-a-sink) |
| Tooling | `echo "\e[31m"` prints `␛[31m` rather than turning the text red, on a pipe and a terminal alike; colour is `Core\Cli\Text` | [`tooling/terminal-output-is-a-sink`](rules/tooling.md#tooling-terminal-output-is-a-sink) |
| Tooling | a hand-rolled `"\e[1m"` literal fails the build instead of styling the output | [`tooling/an-escape-in-a-literal-is-a-compile-error`](rules/tooling.md#tooling-an-escape-in-a-literal-is-a-compile-error) |
| Tooling | there is no escape string and no `<red>…</red>` markup; a style is `Cli\Style::of({...})` over `Cli\Color` values | [`tooling/styling-is-a-value-not-a-grammar`](rules/tooling.md#tooling-styling-is-a-value-not-a-grammar) |
| Tooling | `posix_isatty`, `NO_COLOR` handling and `tput cols` are one profile read at start-up; a program writes `Cli\Text` and never asks what the terminal supports | [`tooling/the-terminal-profile-resolves-once`](rules/tooling.md#tooling-the-terminal-profile-resolves-once) |
| Tooling | `mb_strwidth` counts code points and sees an escape sequence as zero columns; `displayWidth` counts the substituted string, so a control byte costs one column | [`tooling/display-width-measures-what-the-sink-writes`](rules/tooling.md#tooling-display-width-measures-what-the-sink-writes) |
| Tooling | `STDOUT`, `STDERR`, `php://stdout` and `fwrite(STDOUT, …)` have no counterpart; byte-exact output names a file, and standard input is `Core\IO::stdin()` alone | [`tooling/no-raw-handle-onto-standard-output`](rules/tooling.md#tooling-no-raw-handle-onto-standard-output) |
| Tooling | a request handler cannot reach the terminal at all, where PHP-FPM's `STDOUT` quietly lands in the server log | [`tooling/the-tty-belongs-to-the-main-task`](rules/tooling.md#tooling-the-tty-belongs-to-the-main-task) |
| Tooling | there is no `\r`-and-overwrite progress bar and no cursor movement; `Cli::live` and `Cli::progress` hand the body a handle and paint nothing at all on a pipe | [`tooling/in-place-output-is-a-scoped-live-region`](rules/tooling.md#tooling-in-place-output-is-a-scoped-live-region) |
| Tooling | `readline()` reads standard input; `Cli::ask` reads the controlling terminal, so a piped program can still ask a question | [`tooling/a-prompt-is-a-core-member`](rules/tooling.md#tooling-a-prompt-is-a-core-member) |
| Tooling | `readline()` in CI hangs until the pipeline kills it; here it throws, and no `timeout` option lengthens the wait | [`tooling/a-prompt-never-blocks`](rules/tooling.md#tooling-a-prompt-never-blocks) |
| Tooling | a script that dies mid-prompt does not leave the shell in raw mode; restoration is the runtime's obligation rather than a `finally` the author remembers | [`tooling/the-terminal-is-restored-on-every-exit-path`](rules/tooling.md#tooling-the-terminal-is-restored-on-every-exit-path) |
| Tooling | `getopt()` and hand-parsed `$argv` become a table built while compiling; a duplicate command, two options sharing a spelling, or an `#[Option]` on a type no text converts into is a compile error rather than a run-time surprise | [`tooling/commands-are-compiled`](rules/tooling.md#tooling-commands-are-compiled) |
| Tooling | an argument arrives as the parameter's declared type, `uint` unqualified and `string` `tainted`, instead of every option being a string in an array | [`tooling/a-parameter-is-an-argument-unless-it-is-an-option`](rules/tooling.md#tooling-a-parameter-is-an-argument-unless-it-is-an-option) |
| Tooling | nobody writes a usage block or a completion script; `--help` and `bash`/`zsh`/`fish`/`pwsh` completions are read off the compiled table | [`tooling/command-run-dispatches-and-help-is-generated`](rules/tooling.md#tooling-command-run-dispatches-and-help-is-generated) |
| Tooling | there is no `.php-cs-fixer.php`, no ruleset and no style flag; every knob php-cs-fixer and PHP_CodeSniffer expose is one fixed answer here | [`tooling/fmt-is-one-canonical-style`](rules/tooling.md#tooling-fmt-is-one-canonical-style) |
| Tooling | PER's modifier order is enforced rather than recommended, and `else if` is always written `elseif` | [`tooling/fmt-base-style-is-per`](rules/tooling.md#tooling-fmt-base-style-is-per) |
| Tooling | php-cs-fixer and Prettier-style tools re-wrap to a column limit; here there is no line-length rule at all, soft or hard | [`tooling/fmt-never-reflows`](rules/tooling.md#tooling-fmt-never-reflows) |
| Tooling | php-cs-fixer's `trailing_comma_in_multiline` is a choice; here it is the only layout | [`tooling/fmt-trailing-commas`](rules/tooling.md#tooling-fmt-trailing-commas) |
| Tooling | there is no grouped `use A\{B, C};` form to order, because Novis's `use` names exactly one path | [`tooling/fmt-sorts-the-use-block`](rules/tooling.md#tooling-fmt-sorts-the-use-block) |
| Tooling | PHP's case-insensitive keywords are not normalized; `IF` is a legal class name and fixing an identifier's case is a rename, not a layout | [`tooling/fmt-normalizes-only-reserved-spellings`](rules/tooling.md#tooling-fmt-normalizes-only-reserved-spellings) |
| Tooling | php-cs-fixer's `visibility_required` fixer writes the missing `public`; the formatter here never changes meaning, and the insertion happens only in `nvs convert` | [`tooling/fmt-never-inserts-visibility`](rules/tooling.md#tooling-fmt-never-inserts-visibility) |
| Tooling | php-cs-fixer's `ordered_class_elements` has no counterpart; a member's position is kept | [`tooling/fmt-never-reorders-members`](rules/tooling.md#tooling-fmt-never-reorders-members) |
| Tooling | no `php -l`-style check ever holds a stylistic opinion, and formatting never lands in the same report as an error | [`tooling/fmt-is-never-a-diagnostic`](rules/tooling.md#tooling-fmt-is-never-a-diagnostic) |
| Tooling | `php-cs-fixer fix --dry-run` is the habit; the flag is `--check` and its exit status is the whole contract | [`tooling/fmt-check-writes-nothing`](rules/tooling.md#tooling-fmt-check-writes-nothing) |
| Tooling | there is no `/** */` docblock; the PHPDoc shape is an ordinary comment nothing reads | [`tooling/doc-comment-is-three-slashes`](rules/tooling.md#tooling-doc-comment-is-three-slashes) |
| Tooling | there is no `@param`, `@return`, `@throws`, `@var` or `@deprecated`; what PHPDoc tags carried is the signature, an attribute or a declared capability | [`tooling/doc-comment-tags-are-see-and-example`](rules/tooling.md#tooling-doc-comment-tags-are-see-and-example) |
| Tooling | an IDE cannot answer the check with a generated docblock, because there is no tag to generate | [`tooling/strict-docs`](rules/tooling.md#tooling-strict-docs) |
| Tooling | the renderer ships inside the binary rather than as a phpDocumentor-style tool a project installs | [`tooling/nvs-doc-renders-and-decides-nothing`](rules/tooling.md#tooling-nvs-doc-renders-and-decides-nothing) |
| Tooling | phpDocumentor re-derives documentation from source at every run; here nothing does, and the renderers share one JSON | [`tooling/one-json-several-renderers`](rules/tooling.md#tooling-one-json-several-renderers) |
| Tooling | there is no `php --rf`, no reflection dump and no phpDocumentor pass over the standard library; one command from the binary is the reference's only input | [`tooling/meta-json`](rules/tooling.md#tooling-meta-json) |
| Tooling | no PHP binary is needed to convert, and the source is read at one declared dialect between 7.4 and 8.6 rather than under whichever PHP is installed | [`tooling/convert-php-front-end`](rules/tooling.md#tooling-convert-php-front-end) |
| Tooling | a Rector run rewrites in one best-effort pass; here every rewrite is proven, annotated or commented out, and the default output is a worklist that does not run | [`tooling/convert-one-table-two-modes`](rules/tooling.md#tooling-convert-one-table-two-modes) |
| Tooling | a Rector run iterates to a fixpoint and its output depends on the installed PHP; every pass here runs once, in a fixed order, and no PHP binary is consulted | [`tooling/convert-is-deterministic`](rules/tooling.md#tooling-convert-is-deterministic) |
| Tooling | no autoloader, bootstrap or `composer install` runs, and a Composer dependency is reported against the package registry rather than ported | [`tooling/convert-never-does`](rules/tooling.md#tooling-convert-never-does) |
| Tooling | PHP advertises itself through `X-Powered-By` and measures nothing; here nothing leaves the machine unless the operator switched it on | [`tooling/telemetry-is-two-opt-ins`](rules/tooling.md#tooling-telemetry-is-two-opt-ins) |
| Tooling | there is no daemon, no timer and no background process; a server under load makes zero outbound telemetry connections | [`tooling/a-serving-process-never-uploads`](rules/tooling.md#tooling-a-serving-process-never-uploads) |
| The editor | a PHP editor — PhpStorm, Intelephense — carries a parser of its own beside `php`; here the editor parses with the compiler's one grammar, so what the editor accepts and what `nvs check` accepts cannot drift | [`ide/one-grammar-one-tree`](rules/ide.md#ide-one-grammar-one-tree) |
| The editor | an editor over PHP goes dark below the first syntax error until it is fixed; here completion and hover keep working on the well-formed code around it | [`ide/the-tree-survives-a-syntax-error`](rules/ide.md#ide-the-tree-survives-a-syntax-error) |
| The editor | PhpStorm ships a hand-maintained stub tree for PHP's built-ins; here the stubs are generated from the registry the runtime dispatches on, so a stub cannot say what the binary does not do | [`ide/the-stub-tree-is-where-core-is-declared`](rules/ide.md#ide-the-stub-tree-is-where-core-is-declared) |
| The editor | a PHP editor's diagnostics come from one pass with no phase to gate, so a mid-statement typo shows every consequence it cascades into | [`ide/diagnostics-are-phase-gated`](rules/ide.md#ide-diagnostics-are-phase-gated) |
| The editor | there is no inspection profile to tune; a fix exists only where a diagnostic already carries its replacement text, and running fixes on save is `editor.codeActionsOnSave`, never part of the formatter | [`ide/a-quick-fix-is-a-diagnostics-own-suggestion`](rules/ide.md#ide-a-quick-fix-is-a-diagnostics-own-suggestion) |
| The editor | implement-missing-members copies real signatures instead of guessing at them, and there is no getter/setter generator because property hooks make the pair pointless | [`ide/a-code-action-writes-only-what-is-already-determined`](rules/ide.md#ide-a-code-action-writes-only-what-is-already-determined) |
| The editor | PhpStorm's auto-import may add `use Foo as Bar` to dodge a clash; here an alias is not a spelling the language has, so the editor cannot write one | [`ide/no-refactoring-introduces-an-alias`](rules/ide.md#ide-no-refactoring-introduces-an-alias) |
| The editor | the language never infers an array's type from its literal; the narrowing is an editor edit a person reads in a diff and approves | [`ide/narrow-an-annotation-to-its-literal`](rules/ide.md#ide-narrow-an-annotation-to-its-literal) |
| The editor | a value decoded from input stays `array<mixed>` on purpose and gets no offer, where a PHP editor would happily type it from one observed payload | [`ide/the-action-answers-from-the-literal-or-not-at-all`](rules/ide.md#ide-the-action-answers-from-the-literal-or-not-at-all) |
| The editor | type annotations sit where PHP has none — parameters, returns, properties, `foreach` bindings, typed locals, inline shapes — so a borrowed PHP grammar mis-colours the largest part of a Novis file | [`ide/highlighting-is-two-layers`](rules/ide.md#ide-highlighting-is-two-layers) |
| The editor | a PHP grammar colours `===`, `(int)$x` and `if (...): endif;` as syntax; here they render as body text so the editor never confirms what the compiler refuses | [`ide/rejected-syntax-gets-no-colour`](rules/ide.md#ide-rejected-syntax-gets-no-colour) |
| The editor | no PHP tool shows a value's taint at its use sites; here `tainted` and `secret` travel as token modifiers to every use, not only the declaration | [`ide/semantic-tokens-carry-the-qualifiers`](rules/ide.md#ide-semantic-tokens-carry-the-qualifiers) |
| The editor | framework-aware IntelliSense built from convention scans and annotation dialects has no counterpart; a route name or a directive completes from the table the compiler built, a value from outside the program completes from the JSON files in a `.novis/completion/` folder, which do the job of PhpStorm's `.phpstorm.meta.php`, and an ORM column or a view name has nothing to complete from because Novis has neither | [`ide/completion-offers-only-what-the-compiler-derived`](rules/ide.md#ide-completion-offers-only-what-the-compiler-derived) |
| The editor | PhpStorm's `.phpstorm.meta.php` is one PHP file it parses for the same purpose; a completion file is JSON, any number of them may sit in any `.novis/completion/` folder, and any program may write one | [`ide/completion-files-offer-values-at-named-parameters`](rules/ide.md#ide-completion-files-offer-values-at-named-parameters) |
| The editor | typing a PHP built-in's name offers an item that may say dropped, waiting on a milestone or undecided and type nothing, rather than inserting the PHP call | [`ide/three-of-four-item-shapes-insert-nothing`](rules/ide.md#ide-three-of-four-item-shapes-insert-nothing) |
| The editor | the markup half of a file gets Emmet, tag closing, the colour picker and the HTML formatter as in a PHP editor, but each markup chunk is indented from the `?>` that opened it — the Novis block's depth — rather than from the markup's own nesting alone | [`ide/a-template-region-gets-the-editors-services-and-formatter`](rules/ide.md#ide-a-template-region-gets-the-editors-services-and-formatter) |
| The editor | PhpStorm's PHP support is a native PSI plugin with its own formatter and refactorings, whereas its Novis plugin is a bridge to the same server VS Code drives, so nothing about `.nvs` is decided in the editor | [`ide/one-server-two-thin-clients`](rules/ide.md#ide-one-server-two-thin-clients) |
| The editor | a `.nvs` file is not a PHP file to the editor, so Intelephense and PhpStorm's bundled PHP support never open it and none of their settings reach it | [`ide/nvs-is-its-own-file-type`](rules/ide.md#ide-nvs-is-its-own-file-type) |
| The editor | opening a `.php` file gets the PHP extension already installed, not Novis, even though `nvs-syntax` could parse it | [`ide/the-extension-claims-nvs-only`](rules/ide.md#ide-the-extension-claims-nvs-only) |
| The editor | double-clicking `$total` selects `$total`; a configuration borrowed from a PHP extension selects `total` and puts every rename-adjacent interaction off by one character | [`ide/language-configuration-is-content`](rules/ide.md#ide-language-configuration-is-content) |
| The editor | a PHP editor continues a `/** */` docblock and autocompletes tags into it; here the continuation is a `///` run and there is no tag to complete | [`ide/doc-comment-authoring-is-the-editors-own`](rules/ide.md#ide-doc-comment-authoring-is-the-editors-own) |
| The editor | Xdebug's profiler writes cachegrind for KCachegrind or PhpStorm's own viewer; a Novis profile is speedscope JSON and opens in speedscope.app or an embedded view of it | [`ide/the-extension-builds-no-ui-the-editor-already-has`](rules/ide.md#ide-the-extension-builds-no-ui-the-editor-already-has) |
| The editor | Reformat Code runs `nvs fmt` with no PhpStorm Code Style page behind it, and PSI-level refactoring, structural search and the native debugger are absent for `.nvs` | [`ide/phpstorm-bridges-to-the-same-server`](rules/ide.md#ide-phpstorm-bridges-to-the-same-server) |
| The editor | there is no Xdebug-style listener to configure in the editor; the editor points its own debugger UI at `nvs dap` and renders what the adapter reports | [`ide/the-debug-adapter-does-not-wait-for-an-editor`](rules/ide.md#ide-the-debug-adapter-does-not-wait-for-an-editor) |
| The editor | break-on-uncaught and break-on-thrown are two exception filters rather than PHP's five categories, and a spawned isolate appears as a thread rather than as a second session | [`ide/the-debugger-ui-is-as-deep-as-the-adapter`](rules/ide.md#ide-the-debugger-ui-is-as-deep-as-the-adapter) |
| Testing | there is no test framework to install, no naming convention and no base class; a malformed test is a compile error rather than a case that silently never runs | [`testing/test-attribute`](rules/testing.md#testing-test-attribute) |
| Testing | test code is absent from a built artifact by construction, rather than excluded by whatever the deployment happened to copy | [`testing/tests-never-reach-a-build`](rules/testing.md#testing-tests-never-reach-a-build) |
| Testing | total isolation is the default rather than a per-case escape hatch; a static one test wrote is never visible to the next | [`testing/isolate-per-test`](rules/testing.md#testing-isolate-per-test) |
| Testing | there is no reflection to reach a private member with, so white-box testing is bought by co-location and by nothing else | [`testing/private-in-the-same-file`](rules/testing.md#testing-private-in-the-same-file) |
| Testing | the argument order is `(actual, expected)`, the reverse of PHPUnit's, and comparing an `int` against a `string` does not compile | [`testing/assertions-are-typed`](rules/testing.md#testing-assertions-are-typed) |
| Testing | a `catch (Throwable)` around a failing assertion cannot turn a red test green; the runner reads its own ledger rather than the exception state | [`testing/failure-ledger`](rules/testing.md#testing-failure-ledger) |
| Testing | there is no `setUp`, `setUpBeforeClass` or `tearDownAfterClass`; the constructor is the only one, and every property is assigned before any test body runs | [`testing/constructor-is-setup`](rules/testing.md#testing-constructor-is-setup) |
| Testing | shared setup is resolved by declared type while compiling, so an unsatisfiable parameter is a diagnostic rather than a null at run time | [`testing/fixtures`](rules/testing.md#testing-fixtures) |
| Testing | a data provider is a checked attribute payload rather than an `array<array<mixed>>` a method returns, so a row that does not fit the signature is refused where it is written | [`testing/data-rows`](rules/testing.md#testing-data-rows) |
| Testing | no class is generated and no source is evaluated; a double is a value the checker compares against the interface, and a loose or nice double is not expressible | [`testing/doubles`](rules/testing.md#testing-doubles) |
| Testing | there is no `expects()`; the method being asserted on is a compile-checked reference, so renaming it breaks the test rather than leaving it passing | [`testing/interaction-after-the-fact`](rules/testing.md#testing-interaction-after-the-fact) |
| Testing | time and randomness are controlled by a declaration on the test rather than by a clock parameter threaded through every time-aware class | [`testing/determinism-declared-on-the-test`](rules/testing.md#testing-determinism-declared-on-the-test) |
| Testing | an HTTP test needs no socket, no port and no web server; the real route table and the real middleware chain answer it in microseconds | [`testing/in-process-request`](rules/testing.md#testing-in-process-request) |
| Testing | there is no way to intercept `curl_exec` short of a wrapper the application was written around or a stub extension; here one registered answer takes the whole test off the network | [`testing/an-outbound-call-is-answered-from-a-table`](rules/testing.md#testing-an-outbound-call-is-answered-from-a-table) |
| Testing | a test with no assertion is a failure rather than a risky-marked pass, and a case that only passed on a retry never counts as green | [`testing/runner-is-strict`](rules/testing.md#testing-runner-is-strict) |
| Testing | there is no coverage driver to install; the probes are already in every compiled unit, and the flags are PHPUnit's `--coverage-clover` with `--coverage-lcov` beside it | [`testing/coverage-report`](rules/testing.md#testing-coverage-report) |
| Testing | there is no instrumented build and no extension to load; the probes are compiled into every unit and a bit is flipped on a request already in flight | [`testing/debug-probes`](rules/testing.md#testing-debug-probes) |
| Security and isolation | there is no subprocess and no `exec('php …')`; a second script runs in this process, under this request's budget and its own arena | [`security/isolate-shares-nothing`](rules/security.md#security-isolate-shares-nothing) |
| Security and isolation | a spawned unit of work receives no budget of its own; it spends the one the inbound request already holds | [`security/isolate-budget-is-the-trees`](rules/security.md#security-isolate-budget-is-the-trees) |
| Security and isolation | `$_GET` inside an included file is the parent's array; here the accessor throws, because a child is not a request | [`security/request-state-throws-in-an-isolate`](rules/security.md#security-request-state-throws-in-an-isolate) |
| Security and isolation | `shmop`, `sysvshm`, APCu, `putenv`, `setlocale`, `bcscale`, `mb_internal_encoding` and `date_default_timezone_set` have no replacement | [`security/no-cross-request-state`](rules/security.md#security-no-cross-request-state) |
| Security and isolation | FFI, stream wrappers, shared memory and `eval` are absent rather than disabled, so no safety claim downstream needs an "unless it is enabled" | [`security/closed-doors`](rules/security.md#security-closed-doors) |
| Security and isolation | there is no `FFI`, no `dl()` and no `com_dotnet`; wrapping a native library is a wasm component instead | [`security/no-ffi`](rules/security.md#security-no-ffi) |
| Security and isolation | `eval`, a string-argument `assert` and `create_function` do not exist in any spelling | [`security/no-eval`](rules/security.md#security-no-eval) |
| Security and isolation | `phar://`, `php://filter`, `data://` and `http://` are file names that do not exist, not protocols | [`security/a-path-is-not-a-url`](rules/security.md#security-a-path-is-not-a-url) |
| Security and isolation | `ReflectionProperty::setAccessible(true)` and every equivalent are rejected outright, not merely undocumented | [`security/reflection-enforces-visibility`](rules/security.md#security-reflection-enforces-visibility) |
| Security and isolation | there is no `open_basedir`, no `disable_functions` and no safe mode; the runtime cannot reach the OS except through a checked door | [`security/capability-check-at-the-door`](rules/security.md#security-capability-check-at-the-door) |
| Security and isolation | `..` and a planted symlink cannot leave a granted root, because the comparison is made after resolution and never on the text | [`security/path-scope-canonicalise-then-prefix`](rules/security.md#security-path-scope-canonicalise-then-prefix) |
| Security and isolation | `shell_exec`, `system`, `passthru` and the backtick operator do not exist; there is an argv array and a grant | [`security/process-exec-capability`](rules/security.md#security-process-exec-capability) |
| Security and isolation | untrusted input has a type PHP has no way to spell, and a program that mixes it into a sink does not compile | [`security/tainted-qualifier`](rules/security.md#security-tainted-qualifier) |
| Security and isolation | there is no `sanitize()`, no `clean()` and no `filter_var` catch-all; a value safe for HTML is not safe for a path | [`security/launderers-are-sink-named`](rules/security.md#security-launderers-are-sink-named) |
| Security and isolation | `htmlspecialchars($x)` in a string-building position does not compile, because escaping twice is a corruption the type can refuse | [`security/launderer-answers-a-carrier`](rules/security.md#security-launderer-answers-a-carrier) |
| Security and isolation | confidentiality is a type, so a credential reaching a page, a log or an exception message is a compile error | [`security/secret-qualifier`](rules/security.md#security-secret-qualifier) |
| Security and isolation | `echo $apiKey`, `var_dump($key)` and a credential interpolated into an exception message are all compile errors | [`security/secret-sinks-refuse`](rules/security.md#security-secret-sinks-refuse) |
| Security and isolation | `$a == $b` over two credentials is not a timing oracle, and no call site has to remember `hash_equals` | [`security/secret-comparison-is-constant-time`](rules/security.md#security-secret-comparison-is-constant-time) |
| Security and isolation | `CURLOPT_SSL_VERIFYPEER = false` is one line of userland; here the same effect needs the deployment to name the host in a grant and the call to ask for it, and the boot prints every grant that was written | [`security/tls-trust-is-relaxed-only-under-a-host-grant`](rules/security.md#security-tls-trust-is-relaxed-only-under-a-host-grant) |
| Security and isolation | `alg: none` and the RS256-to-HS256 confusion have no code path, because no attacker-supplied string selects a verifier | [`security/algorithm-comes-from-the-key`](rules/security.md#security-algorithm-comes-from-the-key) |
| Security and isolation | no verifier returns a falsy value a loose comparison could read as success | [`security/verification-throws-and-compares-in-constant-time`](rules/security.md#security-verification-throws-and-compares-in-constant-time) |
| Security and isolation | there is no `zip`, no `jku` and no `x5u`, so a token cannot talk the verifier into a fetch or a decompression | [`security/jwe-compact-subset`](rules/security.md#security-jwe-compact-subset) |
| Security and isolation | a token with no `kid` cannot be walked against a key set, so verification costs one signature check whatever the sender wrote | [`security/jws-issued-subset`](rules/security.md#security-jws-issued-subset) |
| Security and isolation | a deployment with nothing configured already rejects a forged `POST` | [`security/csrf-is-on-by-default`](rules/security.md#security-csrf-is-on-by-default) |
| Security and isolation | a Trojan Source payload does not survive the lexer, and there is no attribute that switches the check off | [`security/bidi-predicate`](rules/security.md#security-bidi-predicate) |
| Security and isolation | `password_hash($p, PASSWORD_BCRYPT)` has no spelling; the algorithm is not a parameter | [`security/hash-writes-argon2id-only`](rules/security.md#security-hash-writes-argon2id-only) |
| Security and isolation | `$2x$` is refused rather than emulated, because verifying it means reimplementing `crypt_blowfish`'s overflow | [`security/bcrypt-read-roster`](rules/security.md#security-bcrypt-read-roster) |
| Security and isolation | PHP compares the stored parameters for difference; this answers whether the stored hash is weaker than what `hash` writes now | [`security/needs-rehash-answers-weaker`](rules/security.md#security-needs-rehash-answers-weaker) |
| Security and isolation | `password_verify` answers `false` for a column it cannot read; this throws, so a wrong column wakes an operator | [`security/an-unreadable-stored-hash-throws`](rules/security.md#security-an-unreadable-stored-hash-throws) |
| Concurrency | a PHP request has no concurrency to express at all, and the nearest equivalents — `curl_multi_*`, `pcntl_fork`, an extension's own event loop — have no counterpart here | [`concurrency/one-scheduler`](rules/concurrency.md#concurrency-one-scheduler) |
| Concurrency | PHP has no task, so it has no orphan either; here an unparented task is impossible rather than discouraged | [`concurrency/a-child-belongs-to-the-calling-task`](rules/concurrency.md#concurrency-a-child-belongs-to-the-calling-task) |
| Concurrency | PHP places nothing — a request is one core's worth of work, and its nearest equivalent is another process, which shares not even the compiled code | [`concurrency/on-worker-runs-the-child-on-another-core`](rules/concurrency.md#concurrency-on-worker-runs-the-child-on-another-core) |
| Concurrency | there is no PHP construct that runs several calls at once and hands back their results already typed | [`concurrency/all-answers-a-typed-shape`](rules/concurrency.md#concurrency-all-answers-a-typed-shape) |
| Concurrency | `array_map` runs sequentially; this one runs the callback concurrently and still answers in the input's order | [`concurrency/map-preserves-keys-and-order`](rules/concurrency.md#concurrency-map-preserves-keys-and-order) |
| Concurrency | a wait is bounded by an option on the call rather than by `set_time_limit`, `default_socket_timeout` or an ini setting read from somewhere else | [`concurrency/limit-and-deadline-are-the-only-bounds`](rules/concurrency.md#concurrency-limit-and-deadline-are-the-only-bounds) |
| Concurrency | a PHP script that starts something in the background has no construct that waits for it, so nothing there guarantees this | [`concurrency/nothing-is-still-running-when-a-call-returns`](rules/concurrency.md#concurrency-nothing-is-still-running-when-a-call-returns) |
| Concurrency | the `finally`-shaped cleanup a PHP developer would reach for does not run, and there is nothing to catch | [`concurrency/cancellation-runs-no-user-code`](rules/concurrency.md#concurrency-cancellation-runs-no-user-code) |
| Concurrency | `fastcgi_finish_request` keeps the whole worker busy with no accounting, no cap and no deadline; this keeps the tree, and the tree is still bounded | [`concurrency/after-response-outlives-the-connection`](rules/concurrency.md#concurrency-after-response-outlives-the-connection) |
| Concurrency | output written after `fastcgi_finish_request` is silently discarded; here it is refused, at compile time where the call is statically visible | [`concurrency/deferred-work-cannot-write-the-response`](rules/concurrency.md#concurrency-deferred-work-cannot-write-the-response) |
| Concurrency | there is no queue in front of this and no silent backlog; overload is reported to the request that caused it | [`concurrency/a-full-deferred-executor-throws`](rules/concurrency.md#concurrency-a-full-deferred-executor-throws) |
| Concurrency | APCu, `shmop`, `sysvshm`, `sysvsem` and `sysvmsg` are gone, and there is no ambient place a value can be left for the next request to find | [`concurrency/cross-request-state-is-explicit`](rules/concurrency.md#concurrency-cross-request-state-is-explicit) |
| Concurrency | APCu's segment is shared between every worker of an FPM pool and outlives any one of them; this tier is one process's own memory and goes when that process does | [`concurrency/the-process-tier-is-one-store-per-process`](rules/concurrency.md#concurrency-the-process-tier-is-one-store-per-process) |
| Concurrency | `apcu_add`, `apcu_cas` and `apcu_inc` have no counterpart, so a lock or a counter is not built on the cache at all | [`concurrency/put-and-get-are-the-whole-boundary`](rules/concurrency.md#concurrency-put-and-get-are-the-whole-boundary) |
| Concurrency | APCu's serialize-on-store is a wire format with its own type losses; this is the language's own copy, and it refuses what may not cross rather than mangling it | [`concurrency/a-cached-value-is-copied-across-the-boundary`](rules/concurrency.md#concurrency-a-cached-value-is-copied-across-the-boundary) |
| Concurrency | `apc.shm_size` exhaustion makes a store fail; here the cap forgets an older entry and the write succeeds | [`concurrency/cache-memory-is-charged-to-the-core`](rules/concurrency.md#concurrency-cache-memory-is-charged-to-the-core) |
| Concurrency | an APCu-backed session, lock or rate limit does not port: the local tier is not among the backends, so the miswiring is a configuration error rather than a race | [`concurrency/the-local-tier-cannot-hold-what-must-be-coherent`](rules/concurrency.md#concurrency-the-local-tier-cannot-hold-what-must-be-coherent) |
| Concurrency | there is no counterpart at all: PHP has no confidential type, so a token in APCu or memcached is plaintext by construction | [`concurrency/a-secret-is-cached-only-sealed`](rules/concurrency.md#concurrency-a-secret-is-cached-only-sealed) |
| Concurrency | nothing in PHP coordinates a miss between workers, so a cold key is one fetch per worker and a cached failure is the usual workaround | [`concurrency/a-secret-fill-runs-once-per-process`](rules/concurrency.md#concurrency-a-secret-fill-runs-once-per-process) |
| Concurrency | there is nothing a PHP process can hold across requests, so a connection has no counterpart at all — and it is a root rather than a request that never ends | [`concurrency/a-connection-is-a-root-isolate`](rules/concurrency.md#concurrency-a-connection-is-a-root-isolate) |
| Concurrency | there is no handler object and no closure to hand a socket to; the entry is named at the call site the way a spawned script names one, and its arguments are copied rather than shared | [`concurrency/an-upgrade-is-spawn-shaped`](rules/concurrency.md#concurrency-an-upgrade-is-spawn-shaped) |
| Concurrency | there is no `onMessage` callback and no event registration — suspension has no colour, so a blocking-shaped `while` is the whole program | [`concurrency/a-connection-is-a-loop`](rules/concurrency.md#concurrency-a-connection-is-a-loop) |
| Concurrency | a frame is untrusted by type rather than by convention, so it reaches no sink until it has been validated | [`concurrency/a-peer-frame-is-tainted`](rules/concurrency.md#concurrency-a-peer-frame-is-tainted) |
| Concurrency | the choice is made by lifetime rather than by protocol, and there is no `flush`-in-a-loop shape that keeps a request alive | [`concurrency/a-stream-that-outlives-its-request-is-a-connection`](rules/concurrency.md#concurrency-a-stream-that-outlives-its-request-is-a-connection) |
| Concurrency | there is no unbounded wait to configure your way into: an idle, a lifetime and a send timeout all apply before any configuration is written | [`concurrency/connection-bounds-are-finite`](rules/concurrency.md#concurrency-connection-bounds-are-finite) |
| Concurrency | a deploy does not break what is open — there is no per-request re-read of a file a live connection is standing in | [`concurrency/a-connection-keeps-its-compiled-unit`](rules/concurrency.md#concurrency-a-connection-keeps-its-compiled-unit) |
| Concurrency | a queued job and the database write that justified it commit together, where an application on a broker writes an outbox row and relays it afterwards | [`concurrency/enqueue-commits-with-your-write`](rules/concurrency.md#concurrency-enqueue-commits-with-your-write) |
| Concurrency | the queue is four members of the runtime rather than a framework façade, and what `push` answers is a handle rather than an integer id | [`concurrency/queue-four-members`](rules/concurrency.md#concurrency-queue-four-members) |
| Concurrency | a job is a file rather than a class implementing an interface, and nothing about it is a serialized object graph waiting to be reconstructed | [`concurrency/a-job-names-a-file`](rules/concurrency.md#concurrency-a-job-names-a-file) |
| Concurrency | background work carries its own memory, CPU and time budget, and its permissions can only shrink from those of the code that enqueued it | [`concurrency/a-jobs-budget-and-grants-are-recorded-at-enqueue`](rules/concurrency.md#concurrency-a-jobs-budget-and-grants-are-recorded-at-enqueue) |
| Concurrency | a fleet needs no supervisor, no heartbeat and no coordinator process — the database provides the mutual exclusion | [`concurrency/claiming-is-one-statement`](rules/concurrency.md#concurrency-claiming-is-one-statement) |
| Concurrency | there is no failed state to poll for — a job waiting out its backoff is indistinguishable from one that has not run yet, and "did it fail" is a question about the dead-letter table | [`concurrency/a-job-between-attempts-is-pending`](rules/concurrency.md#concurrency-a-job-between-attempts-is-pending) |
| Concurrency | the guarantee is stated rather than implied, so a job is written to tolerate running twice instead of assuming it will not | [`concurrency/delivery-is-at-least-once`](rules/concurrency.md#concurrency-delivery-is-at-least-once) |
| Concurrency | nothing is discarded silently and nothing retries forever — an exhausted job is a row in a dead-letter table rather than a line in a log | [`concurrency/attempts-are-finite-and-a-dead-letter-is-kept`](rules/concurrency.md#concurrency-attempts-are-finite-and-a-dead-letter-is-kept) |
| Concurrency | exhausting memory in background work is a bounded failed attempt rather than a fatal that takes the process with it | [`concurrency/a-budget-overrun-is-a-failed-attempt`](rules/concurrency.md#concurrency-a-budget-overrun-is-a-failed-attempt) |
| Concurrency | cancelling is a race against a worker rather than a command, and the answer says which side won it | [`concurrency/cancel-is-a-race-it-can-lose`](rules/concurrency.md#concurrency-cancel-is-a-race-it-can-lose) |
| Concurrency | removing queued work is two members of the runtime behind a capability, rather than a framework command or a raw delete against a table the runtime owns | [`concurrency/queue-deletion-is-explicit-and-bounded`](rules/concurrency.md#concurrency-queue-deletion-is-explicit-and-bounded) |
| Concurrency | a job shares nothing with the request that enqueued it — no statics, no session, no superglobals — because it is a fresh isolate rather than the same process continuing | [`concurrency/a-job-runs-as-a-root-isolate`](rules/concurrency.md#concurrency-a-job-runs-as-a-root-isolate) |
| Concurrency | workers are the runtime's own and start from configuration — there is no separate daemon or process manager to install beside the server | [`concurrency/who-runs-a-job-is-configuration`](rules/concurrency.md#concurrency-who-runs-a-job-is-configuration) |
| Concurrency | one process is the whole deployment — there is no process manager, no worker daemon and no cron entry beside it | [`concurrency/one-process-serves-requests-schedules-and-jobs`](rules/concurrency.md#concurrency-one-process-serves-requests-schedules-and-jobs) |
| Concurrency | a credential cannot enter a job payload at all, and taint survives the round trip through the database instead of being laundered by it | [`concurrency/a-payload-refuses-secret-and-keeps-its-qualifiers`](rules/concurrency.md#concurrency-a-payload-refuses-secret-and-keeps-its-qualifiers) |
| Concurrency | losing atomicity between a write and its job is a measured deployment fact rather than an unstated one | [`concurrency/foreign-connection-enqueue-is-counted`](rules/concurrency.md#concurrency-foreign-connection-enqueue-is-counted) |
| Concurrency | cron-style entries and background jobs are two mechanisms with two guarantees, rather than one worker loop doing both | [`concurrency/queued-work-is-not-scheduled-work`](rules/concurrency.md#concurrency-queued-work-is-not-scheduled-work) |
| Concurrency | there is no Redis, SQS or AMQP backend to choose and nothing to configure between the application and its jobs | [`concurrency/no-broker-and-no-driver-interface`](rules/concurrency.md#concurrency-no-broker-and-no-driver-interface) |
| Concurrency | a request that waits on I/O suspends one task and hands its core to another, rather than occupying a process until the kernel answers | [`concurrency/the-parking-contract`](rules/concurrency.md#concurrency-the-parking-contract) |
| Concurrency | a read that would block suspends the task rather than the process, and a socket with bytes already buffered costs one ordinary syscall | [`concurrency/try-the-syscall-then-park`](rules/concurrency.md#concurrency-try-the-syscall-then-park) |
| Concurrency | there is no event loop to install and no extension to pick — readiness is the runtime's own and behaves the same on all three platforms | [`concurrency/the-reactor-reports-readiness`](rules/concurrency.md#concurrency-the-reactor-reports-readiness) |
| Concurrency | there is no `await` and no second spelling of any member that touches I/O — a helper reads a socket with the call it would use on a blocking one | [`concurrency/a-stream-is-an-ordinary-io-stream`](rules/concurrency.md#concurrency-a-stream-is-an-ordinary-io-stream) |
| Concurrency | concurrency costs a stack rather than a process, so one machine holds tasks in the hundred-thousands instead of workers in the hundreds | [`concurrency/a-task-stack-is-reserved-wide-and-pooled`](rules/concurrency.md#concurrency-a-task-stack-is-reserved-wide-and-pooled) |
| Concurrency | deep recursion throws a catchable error at a bound derived from the actual stack, rather than crashing the process or being counted by a configured depth alone | [`concurrency/a-tasks-recursion-limit-comes-from-its-own-stack`](rules/concurrency.md#concurrency-a-tasks-recursion-limit-comes-from-its-own-stack) |
| The Core API | PHP's extension partition tracks 1997 C build engineering and is not inherited — `ctype` and `str_pad` land in the same place | [`core-api/tier-placement`](rules/core-api.md#core-api-tier-placement) |
| The Core API | a misspelled built-in is a compile error naming the member rather than a run-time undefined-function fatal | [`core-api/reserved-namespace`](rules/core-api.md#core-api-reserved-namespace) |
| The Core API | PHP's built-ins have no API at all — argument order, failure signalling and option encoding vary between neighbouring functions in the same extension | [`core-api/shape-rules`](rules/core-api.md#core-api-shape-rules) |
| The Core API | `array_map(f, a)` beside `array_filter(a, f)`, and `in_array`, `str_replace` and `preg_match` disagreeing about haystack-before-needle, all become one order | [`core-api/subject-first`](rules/core-api.md#core-api-subject-first) |
| The Core API | `strlen` is `Core\Str::length`, not `Core\Str::len` | [`core-api/members-are-full-words`](rules/core-api.md#core-api-members-are-full-words) |
| The Core API | PHP checks legal characters and never case, so `snake_case` identifiers do not compile here | [`core-api/identifier-casing`](rules/core-api.md#core-api-identifier-casing) |
| The Core API | unlike Rust's `#[allow(non_snake_case)]` there is no attribute, pragma or per-file opt-out; a name mirroring an external format is renamed or does not compile | [`core-api/casing-has-no-suppression`](rules/core-api.md#core-api-casing-has-no-suppression) |
| The Core API | `function f()`, `const X = 1`, `var $x;` and `readonly int $x;` all fail to compile — PHP's silent `public` has no successor | [`core-api/written-visibility`](rules/core-api.md#core-api-written-visibility) |
| The Core API | PHP 8.4 infers a `public` read side for a bare `private(set)`; that is the same implicit `public` in a different spelling and is refused | [`core-api/asymmetric-visibility-is-a-pair`](rules/core-api.md#core-api-asymmetric-visibility-is-a-pair) |
| The Core API | there is no `JsonSerializable`-style magic hook and no structural encoding of public properties | [`core-api/written-participation`](rules/core-api.md#core-api-written-participation) |
| The Core API | `sort($a)` becomes `$a = Arr::sort($a)`; there are no by-reference mutators, no out-parameters and no in-place variants | [`core-api/nothing-mutates`](rules/core-api.md#core-api-nothing-mutates) |
| The Core API | there is no `DateTime`/`DateTimeImmutable` pair — one type, immutable | [`core-api/no-mutable-immutable-twins`](rules/core-api.md#core-api-no-mutable-immutable-twins) |
| The Core API | `setlocale`, `date_default_timezone_set`, the internal array pointer and every error global are absent; a `Zone` is an argument at every instant↔calendar conversion | [`core-api/no-ambient-state`](rules/core-api.md#core-api-no-ambient-state) |
| The Core API | no member returns `false` to signal failure, no member returns an error code, and there is no `json_last_error` or `error_get_last` | [`core-api/failure-throws`](rules/core-api.md#core-api-failure-throws) |
| The Core API | the procedural twin of every OOP subsystem is gone — `date_*`, `collator_*`, the `fopen` family beside `SplFileObject`, `mysqli` twice | [`core-api/one-paradigm-per-operation`](rules/core-api.md#core-api-one-paradigm-per-operation) |
| The Core API | there is no `$s->length()` and no `$a->map()` — `Core\Str` and `Core\Arr` are the one spelling | [`core-api/no-methods-on-scalars-or-arrays`](rules/core-api.md#core-api-no-methods-on-scalars-or-arrays) |
| The Core API | `fopen($p, "r+b")`, `hash("sha256", …)` and `MB_CASE_TITLE` have no spelling; a closed enum, or a subset of one, takes their place | [`core-api/no-mode-strings`](rules/core-api.md#core-api-no-mode-strings) |
| The Core API | the `sleep`/`usleep`/`time_nanosleep` split does not exist — one parameter takes one `Duration` | [`core-api/units-are-types`](rules/core-api.md#core-api-units-are-types) |
| The Core API | `ARRAY_FILTER_USE_KEY` and `ARRAY_FILTER_USE_BOTH` have nothing to select, and there is no `map`/`mapWithKey` pair | [`core-api/callback-receives-value-and-key`](rules/core-api.md#core-api-callback-receives-value-and-key) |
| The Core API | there are no `bool` flag parameters, no `int` bitmask constants and no positional optional tail longer than one | [`core-api/options-bag`](rules/core-api.md#core-api-options-bag) |
| The Core API | `?T` never means "the key may be absent", and there is no omit-when-null encoding option | [`core-api/required-optional-and-nullable`](rules/core-api.md#core-api-required-optional-and-nullable) |
| The Core API | PHP has no way to ask either question of an argument; here the two are different requests at every `Core` member | [`core-api/omission-is-not-a-written-null`](rules/core-api.md#core-api-omission-is-not-a-written-null) |
| The Core API | PHP spreads clearing across `unset`, `""`, `false` and per-function sentinels; here one spelling means one thing at every member | [`core-api/a-written-null-removes`](rules/core-api.md#core-api-a-written-null-removes) |
| The Core API | there is no `resource`, no integer handle and no `$link`-first convention anywhere in `Core` | [`core-api/a-lifetime-is-an-object`](rules/core-api.md#core-api-a-lifetime-is-an-object) |
| The Core API | `apcu_*` and its shared-memory relatives are gone; the tier a program wants is the member it calls | [`core-api/two-cache-tiers`](rules/core-api.md#core-api-two-cache-tiers) |
| The Core API | `tmpfile`, `tempnam` and `sys_get_temp_dir` collapse into one member, and there is no `temporaryFile` | [`core-api/one-temporary-directory-member`](rules/core-api.md#core-api-one-temporary-directory-member) |
| The Core API | `$_SESSION` does not exist and no member silently starts a session — `session_start` has to be written | [`core-api/session-roster`](rules/core-api.md#core-api-session-roster) |
| The Core API | roughly 1,900 built-ins become about 450 members covering strictly more ground | [`core-api/removals`](rules/core-api.md#core-api-removals) |
| The Core classes | `$argv` and `$argc` do not exist, the elements are `tainted`, and the answer is a process fact rather than a per-isolate one | [`core-classes/cli-arguments`](rules/core-classes.md#core-classes-cli-arguments) |
| The Core classes | Novis's own `$_ARGS` superglobal was retired for the same reason PHP's were — a spawned isolate reads its argument through a member | [`core-classes/script-args`](rules/core-classes.md#core-classes-script-args) |
| The Core classes | `exec`, `system`, `shell_exec`, `passthru`, `popen`, `proc_open` and backticks are all gone, and no flag brings a command line back | [`core-classes/process-is-argv-only`](rules/core-classes.md#core-classes-process-is-argv-only) |
| The Core classes | captured output is `bytes`, so text costs an `as string` that throws on invalid UTF-8 rather than mangling it | [`core-classes/process-run`](rules/core-classes.md#core-classes-process-run) |
| The Core classes | a supplied environment replaces the parent's rather than merging with it | [`core-classes/process-options`](rules/core-classes.md#core-classes-process-options) |
