| The Core classes | a `.bat`, `.cmd` or `.ps1` target does not run at all; a shebang script does, because `execve` reads it without re-parsing anything | [`core-classes/process-refuses-a-shell-target`](rules/core-classes.md#core-classes-process-refuses-a-shell-target) |
| The Core classes | there is no `move_uploaded_file` and no temp file to move — a part is streamed to a path the program chose, and `overwrite` defaults to false | [`core-classes/io-write-stream`](rules/core-classes.md#core-classes-io-write-stream) |
| The Core classes | there is no `tmpfile`, no `sys_get_temp_dir` writing and no `tempnam` — the runtime hands out a directory it owns and reclaims it | [`core-classes/temporary-dir-sweep`](rules/core-classes.md#core-classes-temporary-dir-sweep) |
| The Core classes | there is no modifier that asks for backtracking, and `preg_*`'s silent `false` on a backtrack limit is a catchable throw here | [`core-classes/regex-two-tiers`](rules/core-classes.md#core-classes-regex-two-tiers) |
| The Core classes | Unicode mode is not a flag because `string` is always UTF-8, and `/e` and its relatives are not reintroduced | [`core-classes/regex-syntax`](rules/core-classes.md#core-classes-regex-syntax) |
| The Core classes | output is escaped by the sink rather than by a call the developer remembers, and a runtime-computed string can never become `Markup` through `as` | [`core-classes/html-auto-escape`](rules/core-classes.md#core-classes-html-auto-escape) |
| The Core classes | there is no template literal in PHP; the nearest thing is `<?= ?>` in an inline-HTML region, and this is that rule available in expression position | [`core-classes/html-literal`](rules/core-classes.md#core-classes-html-literal) |
| The Core classes | `htmlspecialchars`'s replacement does not answer a `string`, so its result cannot be concatenated back into one and double-escaped | [`core-classes/html-escape-answers-markup`](rules/core-classes.md#core-classes-html-escape-answers-markup) |
| The Core classes | there is no `LIBXML_*` flag matrix and no document class that flips between recovering and throwing — the two front doors are two classes | [`core-classes/html-parsing`](rules/core-classes.md#core-classes-html-parsing) |
| The Core classes | `DOMDocument`, `SimpleXMLElement`, `XMLReader` and the expat callbacks are four vocabularies for one document — there are two here, they share a node family, and they share no operation | [`core-classes/xml-tree-and-stream`](rules/core-classes.md#core-classes-xml-tree-and-stream) |
| The Core classes | there is no `libxml_disable_entity_loader`, no `LIBXML_NOENT` and no entity loader for either to have switched — a `<!DOCTYPE …>` does not parse at all | [`core-classes/xml-refuses-by-construction`](rules/core-classes.md#core-classes-xml-refuses-by-construction) |
| The Core classes | `is_numeric`, `ctype_digit`, `filter_var(FILTER_VALIDATE_INT)` and their kind have no replacement — the conversion is the test | [`core-classes/validate-has-no-type-predicates`](rules/core-classes.md#core-classes-validate-has-no-type-predicates) |
| The Core classes | there is no generic unwrap; a confidential value leaves its qualifier only through this member or through a function that consumes it and returns something else | [`core-classes/secret-reveal`](rules/core-classes.md#core-classes-secret-reveal) |
| The Core classes | reflection is always present rather than a compiled-in extension, it covers no traits because there are none, and it never widens access | [`core-classes/reflect`](rules/core-classes.md#core-classes-reflect) |
| The Core classes | `token_get_all`'s untyped arrays are replaced by one type per production, and there is no `eval` for a rewritten tree to reach | [`core-classes/ast-is-inert`](rules/core-classes.md#core-classes-ast-is-inert) |
| The Core classes | there is no PDO, no mysqli, no pgsql and no sqlite3 twin, no `quote`/`real_escape_string`, no emulated prepares and no multi-statement query | [`core-classes/db-one-api`](rules/core-classes.md#core-classes-db-one-api) |
| The Core classes | a credential is never a DSN string in program source, and there is no destructor to close a connection — the request teardown does it | [`core-classes/db-connection-is-named`](rules/core-classes.md#core-classes-db-connection-is-named) |
| The Core classes | opening a connection is a granted act rather than a library call, and a hostname reaching `Settings.host` may not be `tainted` | [`core-classes/db-capabilities`](rules/core-classes.md#core-classes-db-capabilities) |
| The Core classes | `LOCAL INFILE` cannot be enabled, TLS verifies fully rather than `prefer`, and the charset is forced to UTF-8 | [`core-classes/db-safe-connection-defaults`](rules/core-classes.md#core-classes-db-safe-connection-defaults) |
| The Core classes | there is no unbuffered-query flag and no per-driver difference in what a second statement on a busy connection does | [`core-classes/db-statement-members`](rules/core-classes.md#core-classes-db-statement-members) |
| The Core classes | an array bound to a placeholder is one value rather than a silently expanded list, and an empty `inList` throws instead of guessing | [`core-classes/db-parameters`](rules/core-classes.md#core-classes-db-parameters) |
| The Core classes | nothing is a string because the text protocol made it one — a `DECIMAL` is a `decimal`, a `BIGINT UNSIGNED` is a `uint`, and `TINYINT(1)` holding `7` refuses to read as `bool` | [`core-classes/db-column-types`](rules/core-classes.md#core-classes-db-column-types) |
| The Core classes | there is no `beginTransaction`/`commit`/`rollBack` on the connection and no `inTransaction`; nesting is a savepoint, and a rollback signal survives an intervening `catch (Throwable)` | [`core-classes/db-transactions`](rules/core-classes.md#core-classes-db-transactions) |
| The Core classes | an application branches on `ErrorKind::UniqueViolation` rather than on `1062`, `23505` or the text `"Duplicate entry"` | [`core-classes/db-error`](rules/core-classes.md#core-classes-db-error) |
| The Core classes | there is no version number, no history table, no `up`/`down` pair and no fleet lock — the plan is recomputed from the database every time | [`core-classes/schema-converges`](rules/core-classes.md#core-classes-schema-converges) |
| The Core classes | no class is serialisable by being a class — a wire format is opted into at the declaration, and visibility never decides what is encoded | [`core-classes/derive-attribute`](rules/core-classes.md#core-classes-derive-attribute) |
| The Core classes | a decode failure is one throw carrying a located list, not the first problem the parser happened to hit | [`core-classes/derive-reports-every-field`](rules/core-classes.md#core-classes-derive-reports-every-field) |
| The Core classes | there is no broker, no daemon of its own and no implicit boot-time DDL — the tables are created by `nvs queue migrate` and by nothing else | [`core-classes/queue-storage-is-a-table`](rules/core-classes.md#core-classes-queue-storage-is-a-table) |
| The Core classes | `$_SESSION` does not exist, nothing starts a session implicitly, and a member called before `start` throws | [`core-classes/session-is-started-explicitly`](rules/core-classes.md#core-classes-session-is-started-explicitly) |
| The Core classes | there is no per-IP or per-path limiting, no `[ratelimit]` config block and no middleware writing a `429` for you | [`core-classes/ratelimit-two-members`](rules/core-classes.md#core-classes-ratelimit-two-members) |
| The Core classes | there is no cipher name in a string and no unauthenticated mode to reach for, so `aes-256-ecb` has no spelling | [`core-classes/crypto-interop-tier`](rules/core-classes.md#core-classes-crypto-interop-tier) |
| The Core classes | there is no string to assemble and therefore nothing for two sides to disagree about, and a verified payload comes back `tainted` | [`core-classes/signature`](rules/core-classes.md#core-classes-signature) |
| The Core classes | there is no `parse_url`/`http_build_query` round trip to lose a component in — removing one is a written `null`, and an empty query is a different value from no query | [`core-classes/uri-removable-components`](rules/core-classes.md#core-classes-uri-removable-components) |
| The Core classes | `$max_length` was optional and defaulted to unlimited, so the safe call was the one the caller had to remember to write | [`core-classes/decompression-bound`](rules/core-classes.md#core-classes-decompression-bound) |
| The Core classes | gd's mutable resource and its ambient mode flags are gone; an operation answers a new value, and the component's entry points are coarse by rule | [`core-classes/image-pipeline`](rules/core-classes.md#core-classes-image-pipeline) |
| The Core classes | there are no palette images, no `imagesetpixel`, no drawing primitives and no `imageaffine` — four named transforms cover the affine cases a web application reaches for | [`core-classes/image-pixel-model`](rules/core-classes.md#core-classes-image-pixel-model) |
| The Core classes | TIFF, BMP, TGA, ICO, PNM, HEIC and gd's own formats are not readable at all, and JPEG XL decodes without encoding | [`core-classes/image-format-roster`](rules/core-classes.md#core-classes-image-format-roster) |
| The Core classes | a decompression bomb is refused from its declared dimensions rather than discovered by exhausting memory | [`core-classes/image-pixel-cap`](rules/core-classes.md#core-classes-image-pixel-cap) |
| The Core classes | a phone photo is upright and a CMYK JPEG is sRGB without the caller knowing the tags exist, and location data does not survive a re-encode | [`core-classes/image-correct-by-default`](rules/core-classes.md#core-classes-image-correct-by-default) |
| The Core classes | the SSRF and local-file-read class that defines PHP's HTML-to-PDF libraries is absent by construction — there is nothing in the sandbox to fetch with | [`core-classes/pdf-render-has-no-io`](rules/core-classes.md#core-classes-pdf-render-has-no-io) |
| The Core classes | there is no second FPDF-shaped imperative engine with its own coordinate model — drawings are inline SVG | [`core-classes/pdf-one-engine`](rules/core-classes.md#core-classes-pdf-one-engine) |
| The Core classes | rasterising a page needs no Imagick, no Ghostscript and no shell — it is `Image::open` with a `page` and a `dpi` | [`core-classes/pdf-page-is-an-image-source`](rules/core-classes.md#core-classes-pdf-page-is-an-image-source) |
| The Core classes | an external workbook reference, a linked image and a remote data connection come back as data, and VBA is enumerable payload that never runs | [`core-classes/spreadsheet-has-no-io`](rules/core-classes.md#core-classes-spreadsheet-has-no-io) |
| The Core classes | a string beginning `=`, `+`, `-` or `@` writes as text, so formula injection is closed by type rather than by a remembered quote prefix | [`core-classes/spreadsheet-formula-is-a-value`](rules/core-classes.md#core-classes-spreadsheet-formula-is-a-value) |
| The Core classes | there is no per-cell accessor to loop over, which is the shape most PhpSpreadsheet code takes | [`core-classes/spreadsheet-bulk-boundary`](rules/core-classes.md#core-classes-spreadsheet-bulk-boundary) |
| Observability | there is no APM extension in the request path and no userland StatsD or OpenTelemetry client to reconcile with it; the runtime's own probes are the only instrumentation | [`observability/the-runtime-exports-what-it-already-measures`](rules/observability.md#observability-the-runtime-exports-what-it-already-measures) |
| Observability | there is no `X-Request-ID` read or minted; the W3C trace id is the request identifier a log line, an error rendering and a proxy all share | [`observability/a-trace-id-exists-for-every-request`](rules/observability.md#observability-a-trace-id-exists-for-every-request) |
| Observability | `error_log` writes no correlation id; every JSON-Lines record written inside a traced request can be joined to its trace from the line alone | [`observability/a-log-record-carries-trace-ids-when-a-trace-is-active`](rules/observability.md#observability-a-log-record-carries-trace-ids-when-a-trace-is-active) |
| Observability | there is no client library to install and no `record(name, value, kind)`; a counter, a histogram and a gauge are three members, and a name is validated at a literal call site | [`observability/metrics-three-members`](rules/observability.md#observability-metrics-three-members) |
| Observability | request rate, latency, query time, GC pause and spawn overhead are on the scrape endpoint before the application emits anything, where PHP needs an APM agent or a hand-written StatsD client for the first three and cannot reach the last two at all | [`observability/default-series`](rules/observability.md#observability-default-series) |
| Observability | recording one name as a counter here and a gauge there is a throw at the second call, not a series the backend quietly reports twice | [`observability/a-name-is-fixed-to-one-kind`](rules/observability.md#observability-a-name-is-fixed-to-one-kind) |
| Observability | a series is keyed by the route's compiled name rather than by the request path a StatsD client would key on, so `/users/1`, `/users/2` is one series and not one per user | [`observability/route-label-is-the-declared-name`](rules/observability.md#observability-route-label-is-the-declared-name) |
| Observability | there is no APCu-style shared counter store; every core keeps its own approximate aggregate and the merge is arithmetic at scrape time | [`observability/a-registry-is-per-core-and-nothing-reads-it`](rules/observability.md#observability-a-registry-is-per-core-and-nothing-reads-it) |
| Observability | past the cap the newest label set is dropped with a warning, not the oldest evicted; a counter never appears to reset | [`observability/past-max-series-a-new-series-is-refused`](rules/observability.md#observability-past-max-series-a-new-series-is-refused) |
| Observability | a request cannot switch tracing on for itself the way `xdebug_start_trace()` or an `ini_set` can; where telemetry ships is the deployment's decision | [`observability/metrics-and-trace-blocks-are-system`](rules/observability.md#observability-metrics-and-trace-blocks-are-system) |
| Observability | a distributed trace is not Xdebug's per-call function trace; a span is a request, a query, an outbound call or a spawn, and nothing finer | [`observability/four-kinds-become-a-span`](rules/observability.md#observability-four-kinds-become-a-span) |
| Observability | an OpenTelemetry SDK installed as a library lets a program open a span around any function; here the set of things that become a span is closed and a function call is not in it | [`observability/a-call-never-becomes-a-span`](rules/observability.md#observability-a-call-never-becomes-a-span) |
| Observability | Xdebug's trace is a log of function calls; here a collector pause, an isolate spawn and a database statement are events of their own on the same stream, tagged so a viewer can tell them apart | [`observability/trace-events-carry-a-kind`](rules/observability.md#observability-trace-events-carry-a-kind) |
| Observability | there are no mysqlnd statistics and no general query log; a statement is a trace event, filed in the driver and off the hot path, and it never carries a bound value | [`observability/a-query-is-a-trace-event`](rules/observability.md#observability-a-query-is-a-trace-event) |
| Observability | the slow-query log is a per-connection threshold in `nvs.toml` written by the application's operator, not the server's `slow_query_log`, and it reports the same facts the trace does | [`observability/a-slow-query-is-logged-past-a-threshold`](rules/observability.md#observability-a-slow-query-is-logged-past-a-threshold) |
| Observability | a trace crosses a service boundary with no header code in the application, where a PHP client has to be wrapped to carry one | [`observability/an-outbound-call-propagates-traceparent`](rules/observability.md#observability-an-outbound-call-propagates-traceparent) |
| Observability | there is no Xdebug cachegrind file to open in a bespoke viewer; the timeline is speedscope's open evented format, the same file the sampling profiler writes | [`observability/speedscope-timeline-export`](rules/observability.md#observability-speedscope-timeline-export) |
| Observability | there is no `$real_usage` boolean and no second accounting behind it: `memory_get_usage`'s two numbers were one member with a flag, where the request's held bytes and the process's resident set are two members on the two classes that own them | [`observability/memory-is-three-numbers-on-core-budget`](rules/observability.md#observability-memory-is-three-numbers-on-core-budget) |
| Observability | `memory_get_peak_usage` reads a mark PHP keeps because its allocator holds its chunks; here the mark is kept deliberately, because deterministic release means the current figure falls back to the baseline and hides the spike | [`observability/a-memory-peak-is-recorded-not-asked-for`](rules/observability.md#observability-a-memory-peak-is-recorded-not-asked-for) |
| Observability | PHP has no warning short of the fatal: a request that touched 96% of `memory_limit` and returned successfully is indistinguishable from one that never passed 30% | [`observability/memory-high-water-writes-a-warn`](rules/observability.md#observability-memory-high-water-writes-a-warn) |
| Observability | `register_shutdown_function` is gone; the hook takes a typed `Script\ExitReport` with the reason, the status and the live `Throwable`, where PHP reads `error_get_last()` | [`observability/script-on-exit`](rules/observability.md#observability-script-on-exit) |
| Observability | PHP's shutdown functions fire on most fatals; here a resource-limit `FATAL` reaches only `Core\Fatal::onLimit`, and a migrator moves that one use there | [`observability/a-fatal-and-a-cancellation-run-no-exit-hook`](rules/observability.md#observability-a-fatal-and-a-cancellation-run-no-exit-hook) |
| Observability | a shutdown function in PHP can call `exit` to change the status or silently swallow the pending error; here neither is possible | [`observability/a-hook-observes-and-never-steers`](rules/observability.md#observability-a-hook-observes-and-never-steers) |
| The HTTP server | there is no php-fpm and no FastCGI: the origin speaks HTTP/1.1 over TCP or a Unix socket, terminates no TLS and compresses nothing, so nginx's `fastcgi_pass` becomes `proxy_pass` | [`http-server/two-deployments-and-nothing-a-proxy-owns`](rules/http-server.md#http-server-two-deployments-and-nothing-a-proxy-owns) |
| The HTTP server | `listen` is the origin's own address rather than a php-fpm pool's, and `workers` counts accept cores rather than sizing a `pm.*` process pool | [`http-server/the-server-block-is-boot-class`](rules/http-server.md#http-server-the-server-block-is-boot-class) |
| The HTTP server | a vhost's rewrite rules become one `[[server.mount]]` block, and a module is relocatable because the matched prefix is stripped before the route table sees the path | [`http-server/a-mount-table-expands-at-boot`](rules/http-server.md#http-server-a-mount-table-expands-at-boot) |
| The HTTP server | the same `listen = /run/nvs.sock` shape as php-fpm, but a Windows host has no named-pipe equivalent and listens on TCP loopback | [`http-server/a-unix-socket-listener`](rules/http-server.md#http-server-a-unix-socket-listener) |
| The HTTP server | there is no `php.ini-development` to copy: a production host that wrote nothing is unreachable from code, and one root-owned line opens it | [`http-server/the-mode-ceiling-defaults-to-the-startup-mode`](rules/http-server.md#http-server-the-mode-ceiling-defaults-to-the-startup-mode) |
| The HTTP server | `php -S 0.0.0.0:8000` says nothing; here the bind is announced on the console and in the log stream, and it is not refused | [`http-server/a-development-server-on-a-public-interface-warns-and-serves`](rules/http-server.md#http-server-a-development-server-on-a-public-interface-warns-and-serves) |
| The HTTP server | php-fpm behind nginx ships no security headers, no cookie flags and no outbound timeout until somebody writes them; here nothing written is already the safe and finite configuration | [`http-server/an-unsafe-or-unbounded-default-is-a-defect`](rules/http-server.md#http-server-an-unsafe-or-unbounded-default-is-a-defect) |
| The HTTP server | php-fpm sizes a pool of request *processes* with `pm.*`; `workers` counts accept cores, and one core answers many requests at once | [`http-server/the-accept-fan-out-is-one-worker-per-core`](rules/http-server.md#http-server-the-accept-fan-out-is-one-worker-per-core) |

| The HTTP server | `max_execution_time` and `request_terminate_timeout` bound a whole request; these bound a stalled socket only, so a slow 2 GB upload completes while a stalled one is closed | [`http-server/four-idle-waits-all-finite`](rules/http-server.md#http-server-four-idle-waits-all-finite) |
| The HTTP server | `try_files $uri /index.php` is the development sequence only; in production a URL naming an existing `.nvs` file still runs the mount's entry | [`http-server/a-request-resolves-in-five-steps`](rules/http-server.md#http-server-a-request-resolves-in-five-steps) |

| The HTTP server | `X-Real-IP`, `CF-Connecting-IP`, `True-Client-IP`, `Fastly-Client-IP`, `X-Client-IP` and RFC 7239 `Forwarded` are never read, so the common `proxy_set_header X-Real-IP` recipe alone leaves every client as the proxy | [`http-server/x-forwarded-for-is-the-only-address-header`](rules/http-server.md#http-server-x-forwarded-for-is-the-only-address-header) |

| The HTTP server | there is no `X-Request-ID` and no `$_SERVER['UNIQUE_ID']`; the W3C trace id is the one identifier on every log line, error page and response | [`http-server/the-trace-id-is-the-request-identifier`](rules/http-server.md#http-server-the-trace-id-is-the-request-identifier) |
| The HTTP server | there is no Common or Combined Log Format and no pool `access.log`: the line is a diagnostic record, text in development and JSON in production | [`http-server/the-access-log-is-a-mode-default`](rules/http-server.md#http-server-the-access-log-is-a-mode-default) |

| The HTTP server | `setcookie` defaults to no `Secure`, no `HttpOnly` and no `SameSite`; here every cookie starts with all three, `SameSite` is an enum rather than a string, and a script-readable cookie is one written field at the call | [`http-server/cookies-are-secure-httponly-and-lax`](rules/http-server.md#http-server-cookies-are-secure-httponly-and-lax) |
| The HTTP server | there is no `SessionHandlerInterface` and no `validateId`; an id the store never issued, one that expired and one an attacker minted are all the same absent answer, and `start` issues a fresh record for each | [`http-server/a-session-store-answers-four-operations`](rules/http-server.md#http-server-a-session-store-answers-four-operations) |
| The HTTP server | `session.save_handler = files` and an APCu-backed handler have no counterpart; the choices are the shared tier or the database, and `local` is `E0626` where it is written rather than a session that forgets people | [`http-server/session-backend-is-shared-or-db-and-local-is-refused-at-boot`](rules/http-server.md#http-server-session-backend-is-shared-or-db-and-local-is-refused-at-boot) |
| The HTTP server | `session_start()` with nothing configured writes files under `session.save_path`; here a store nobody chose is no store, and the first `start` says which block would choose one | [`http-server/no-session-block-means-no-store`](rules/http-server.md#http-server-no-session-block-means-no-store) |
| The HTTP server | PHP holds an exclusive lock on the session for the length of the request, so two requests from one browser serialize; here there is no lock, and two concurrent writes to one session are last-write-wins over the whole record | [`http-server/a-session-is-loaded-once-and-written-whole`](rules/http-server.md#http-server-a-session-is-loaded-once-and-written-whole) |
| The HTTP server | `session.gc_probability` and `session.gc_divisor` have no counterpart, because both backends can expire an entry themselves and a filesystem cannot | [`http-server/session-expiry-belongs-to-the-store`](rules/http-server.md#http-server-session-expiry-belongs-to-the-store) |
| The HTTP server | `$_SESSION` holds whatever it is given in the clear, and a token in it is readable by anything that can read the store | [`http-server/a-session-holds-a-secret-only-sealed`](rules/http-server.md#http-server-a-session-holds-a-secret-only-sealed) |
| The HTTP server | there is no `$_FILES` array and no buffered accessor beside the iterator; every application that accepts a file writes a `foreach`, and a part's bytes are readable once, in order | [`http-server/an-upload-is-received-only-through-files`](rules/http-server.md#http-server-an-upload-is-received-only-through-files) |
| The HTTP server | a part answers `name()`, `filename()` and `contentType()` as tainted strings through members, and there is no `size`, no `tmp_name` and no `error` slot | [`http-server/a-part-is-a-file-iff-it-carries-a-filename`](rules/http-server.md#http-server-a-part-is-a-file-iff-it-carries-a-filename) |
| The HTTP server | `move_uploaded_file` is `saveTo`, `file_get_contents($tmp)` is `readAll` under `request_body`, and a second pass over an upload has to say where the first one put it | [`http-server/a-part-is-consumed-in-one-of-three-ways`](rules/http-server.md#http-server-a-part-is-consumed-in-one-of-three-ways) |
| The HTTP server | `upload_max_filesize` and `post_max_size` are replaced by a cap on what is parsed into memory and a cap on what is streamed past it, and a file's size is never checked against the first | [`http-server/request-body-and-upload-total-are-two-caps`](rules/http-server.md#http-server-request-body-and-upload-total-are-two-caps) |
| The HTTP server | there is no `tmp_name`, no `upload_tmp_dir`, no `move_uploaded_file` and no `is_uploaded_file`; an upload nobody saves is never on disk, and one that is saved is there because the program wrote it | [`http-server/there-is-no-temp-file`](rules/http-server.md#http-server-there-is-no-temp-file) |
| The HTTP server | curl defaults to no timeout and `file_get_contents` to `default_socket_timeout`'s sixty seconds; here there is no `null`, no `0` and no option that means unbounded, so a long call names its own `deadline` | [`http-server/no-spelling-for-an-unbounded-wait`](rules/http-server.md#http-server-no-spelling-for-an-unbounded-wait) |
| The HTTP server | curl takes `CURLOPT_POSTFIELDS` as a string, an array or a file handle and infers the encoding from which one it got; here the key names what is sent, two keys are refused before the program runs, and a `Part::file` streams from disk rather than being held whole | [`http-server/an-outbound-request-carries-one-body`](rules/http-server.md#http-server-an-outbound-request-carries-one-body) |
| The HTTP server | curl's `CURLOPT_TIMEOUT` bounds one transfer, so three attempts at five seconds is a fifteen-second call; here the stated number is the bound on everything | [`http-server/one-deadline-covers-the-whole-call`](rules/http-server.md#http-server-one-deadline-covers-the-whole-call) |
| The HTTP server | a PHP stream has `default_socket_timeout` and nothing that bounds how long a body may take; here a streamed body has two finite bounds it cannot be without, and reading it twice throws | [`http-server/a-streamed-reply-is-bounded-by-idle-and-a-lifetime`](rules/http-server.md#http-server-a-streamed-reply-is-bounded-by-idle-and-a-lifetime) |
| The HTTP server | PHP's clients have no retry, so every application writes its own loop; here it is three flat options, the jitter is not configurable, and a `Retry-After` header replaces the computed wait | [`http-server/retry-is-opt-in-jittered-and-closed`](rules/http-server.md#http-server-retry-is-opt-in-jittered-and-closed) |
| The HTTP server | a retried `POST` in PHP does whatever the loop the developer wrote does, including charging a card twice; here the missing key is a red squiggle before the program runs | [`http-server/a-non-idempotent-retry-needs-an-idempotency-key`](rules/http-server.md#http-server-a-non-idempotent-retry-needs-an-idempotency-key) |
| The HTTP server | `file_get_contents($userUrl)` and `curl_setopt(CURLOPT_URL, $userUrl)` are a compile-time diagnostic, and the laundered value is a `Target` the program cannot read an address back out of, not a string | [`http-server/allow-url-pins-the-address`](rules/http-server.md#http-server-allow-url-pins-the-address) |
| The HTTP server | curl tries every address a name answers and checks none of them; here each is checked before any is tried, one denied refuses the whole host, and the lookup runs off the core | [`http-server/an-outbound-call-tries-every-approved-address`](rules/http-server.md#http-server-an-outbound-call-tries-every-approved-address) |
| The HTTP server | `CURLOPT_RESOLVE` takes any host-to-address mapping a script writes; here the host must be granted, the address is judged by the same policy a resolved one is, and the certificate is still checked against the URL's host | [`http-server/an-outbound-call-names-its-address-only-under-a-grant`](rules/http-server.md#http-server-an-outbound-call-names-its-address-only-under-a-grant) |
| The HTTP server | curl's `FOLLOWLOCATION` is off by default too, but a hop it follows is never checked against anything; here each hop passes the same policy the first URL did and a denied one fails the call rather than being dropped from the chain | [`http-server/redirects-are-off-and-every-hop-is-re-pinned`](rules/http-server.md#http-server-redirects-are-off-and-every-hop-is-re-pinned) |
| The HTTP server | curl follows a hop from `https` to `http` silently, so one `Location` header strips a call's TLS; here it needs a grant and a call-site option, and the refusal names the grant | [`http-server/an-https-redirect-never-becomes-plaintext`](rules/http-server.md#http-server-an-https-redirect-never-becomes-plaintext) |
| The HTTP server | an `Authorization` header set in a stream context is re-sent to whatever host a `Location` names; here a hop to another origin carries no header the program wrote, that one and every `secret` value included | [`http-server/a-cross-origin-redirect-drops-credentials`](rules/http-server.md#http-server-a-cross-origin-redirect-drops-credentials) |
| The HTTP server | curl reuses a connection keyed on host and port inside one handle, and PHP's stream functions reuse nothing; here the key carries the pinned address, the client identity and the call's TLS policy, so reuse cannot widen what a check approved | [`http-server/an-outbound-connection-is-pooled-per-core-and-stays-pinned`](rules/http-server.md#http-server-an-outbound-connection-is-pooled-per-core-and-stays-pinned) |
| The HTTP server | curl and PHP's stream wrappers take a proxy from `HTTP_PROXY`/`HTTPS_PROXY` in the environment, or per handle from `CURLOPT_PROXY`; here it is one root-owned block, no environment variable is read, and no program-side spelling exists | [`http-server/an-outbound-proxy-is-operator-configured`](rules/http-server.md#http-server-an-outbound-proxy-is-operator-configured) |
| The HTTP server | curl hands the proxy the destination's host name in every case, having no approved address to hand it; here that is one of two written answers, the other tunnels to the address the check approved, and the one that gives up the pin is announced at every boot | [`http-server/a-proxied-call-keeps-its-pin-unless-the-operator-says-otherwise`](rules/http-server.md#http-server-a-proxied-call-keeps-its-pin-unless-the-operator-says-otherwise) |
| The HTTP server | `curl.cainfo` and `openssl.cafile` are `ini` settings a script can widen with `ini_set`; here the three keys are `System` class and no code-side spelling for any of them exists | [`http-server/the-client-trust-roots-are-the-operators`](rules/http-server.md#http-server-the-client-trust-roots-are-the-operators) |
| The HTTP server | `curl_getinfo` answers a flat array of thirty-odd keys mixing timings, sizes and TLS facts; here the session is an object read through members and the timings are the trace's | [`http-server/a-reply-reports-its-tls-session`](rules/http-server.md#http-server-a-reply-reports-its-tls-session) |
| The HTTP server | there is no outbound WebSocket in PHP's standard library at all — `ext-sockets` and a userland client are what a program reaches for, and neither passes an address policy | [`http-server/an-outbound-socket-is-opened-like-an-outbound-call`](rules/http-server.md#http-server-an-outbound-socket-is-opened-like-an-outbound-call) |
| The HTTP server | there is no worker process per request to die and be respawned; a request is contained in-process and the process boundary is reserved for one named residue | [`http-server/a-requests-blast-radius-is-bounded-at-four-tiers`](rules/http-server.md#http-server-a-requests-blast-radius-is-bounded-at-four-tiers) |
| The HTTP server | `max_execution_time` fires between statements; here a deadline also reaches inside one `Core` call over a large value, and reaches it by a flag rather than a clock | [`http-server/time-is-bounded-inside-a-helper`](rules/http-server.md#http-server-time-is-bounded-inside-a-helper) |
| The HTTP server | PHP-FPM learns of a closed tab at the script's next write and holds the worker until `max_execution_time`; here the connection's drop is an event, the tree is cancelled and no worker was ever held | [`http-server/an-abandoned-request-is-cancelled-at-the-drop`](rules/http-server.md#http-server-an-abandoned-request-is-cancelled-at-the-drop) |
| The HTTP server | there is no per-request worker process to absorb an engine crash; a fault of this class loses every request in flight and is answered by a restart in about a cold start | [`http-server/the-residue-is-one-named-fault-class`](rules/http-server.md#http-server-the-residue-is-one-named-fault-class) |
| Routing | there is no runtime registry and no routes file — a `$router->get(...)` call has no counterpart, and a duplicate route, an unbound placeholder or a stale link name fails the build rather than a request | [`routing/routes-are-compiled-not-registered`](rules/routing.md#routing-routes-are-compiled-not-registered) |
| Routing | the attribute is read while compiling rather than by a reflection scan at boot, a route's name is never derived from the class and method, and there is no class-level prefix attribute | [`routing/route-attribute`](rules/routing.md#routing-route-attribute) |
| Routing | `{name}` rather than `:name`, a capture is always a whole segment so `/u{id}` and `/{id}.json` are refused rather than partially matched, and there is no inline constraint — the parameter's type is the constraint | [`routing/path-grammar`](rules/routing.md#routing-path-grammar) |
| Routing | `Route::any()` and `methods: ['*']` have no spelling — each verb a route answers is its own `#[Route]` line, because `Allow:` and the CSRF classification read the exact set | [`routing/no-wildcard-verb`](rules/routing.md#routing-no-wildcard-verb) |
| Routing | a routes file is not read top to bottom — first-match-wins does not exist, so moving a declaration between files cannot change which route answers | [`routing/precedence-is-structural`](rules/routing.md#routing-precedence-is-structural) |
| Routing | there is no `->where('lang', 'en|de|fr')`; the constraint is the parameter's type, and a regex on a route is refused outright | [`routing/a-capture-narrows-to-a-closed-set`](rules/routing.md#routing-a-capture-narrows-to-a-closed-set) |
| Routing | there is no backed-versus-pure split to route on — every enum is integer-backed, so what decides the spelling is whether the value was written | [`routing/an-enum-capture-is-spelled-by-its-backing-value-or-its-case-name`](rules/routing.md#routing-an-enum-capture-is-spelled-by-its-backing-value-or-its-case-name) |
| Routing | an optional segment is declared by the parameter's default, not by a second route or an optional regex group, and `/posts/` does not match `/posts/{page?}` | [`routing/a-trailing-segment-may-be-absent`](rules/routing.md#routing-a-trailing-segment-may-be-absent) |
| Routing | a query key is declared on the handler's parameter with a type, matched nominally as `Core\Query`, rather than read out of `$_GET` and validated by hand | [`routing/a-query-parameter-is-declared-like-a-capture`](rules/routing.md#routing-a-query-parameter-is-declared-like-a-capture) |
| Routing | a bad query value is refused with a 400 before the handler sees it, instead of arriving as a string the handler casts and checks | [`routing/a-bad-query-value-is-a-400`](rules/routing.md#routing-a-bad-query-value-is-a-400) |
| Routing | a framework's `methods: ['POST', 'PUT']` on one named route becomes one `#[Route]` line per verb, each carrying the same `name` and the same `path` | [`routing/repeated-routes-share-a-name-when-they-share-a-path`](rules/routing.md#routing-repeated-routes-share-a-name-when-they-share-a-path) |
| Routing | the generated `operationId` is the route name, suffixed with the lowercased verb only where two operations share it — never a counter | [`routing/a-shared-name-is-one-endpoint-everywhere`](rules/routing.md#routing-a-shared-name-is-one-endpoint-everywhere) |
| Routing | no framework router's dispatch is here — no controller base class, no middleware, no return-value-to-response rule, no `HEAD`-implies-`GET` or trailing-slash normalisation; the program or its framework writes the `switch` | [`routing/matching-is-not-dispatching`](rules/routing.md#routing-matching-is-not-dispatching) |
| Routing | there is no `$route->getCallable()`; the handler is reached by a `switch` the framework generates or the application writes | [`routing/a-match-is-not-invocable`](rules/routing.md#routing-a-match-is-not-invocable) |
| Routing | the match is made by the server and read off the request, not by a framework kernel in userland that matches and then calls the controller | [`routing/matched-once-before-the-handler`](rules/routing.md#routing-matched-once-before-the-handler) |
| Routing | a matched route never calls anything; the program or the framework dispatches, and a `null` route is a fact the program reads rather than a 404 anything sends | [`routing/the-servers-match-dispatches-nothing`](rules/routing.md#routing-the-servers-match-dispatches-nothing) |
| Routing | a wrong verb on a known path is a 405 with an `Allow:` list asked of the table, rather than the 404 a hand-rolled dispatch falls into | [`routing/a-refused-verb-is-not-a-missing-path`](rules/routing.md#routing-a-refused-verb-is-not-a-missing-path) |
| Routing | the deployment prefix is never derived from `REQUEST_URI` or `SCRIPT_NAME`; the server hands it over, and a tenant is a mount capture rather than a `host` field on the route | [`routing/a-request-reads-its-mount`](rules/routing.md#routing-a-request-reads-its-mount) |
| Routing | a link is built from the route's name and checked while compiling, never assembled by hand — a renamed route fails the build at every stale `url()` rather than in a sent email | [`routing/link-name-and-params-are-checked`](rules/routing.md#routing-link-name-and-params-are-checked) |
| Routing | a link is never the declared path concatenated by hand, because the path a route is declared against is the mount-stripped one and the prefix is known only where the request is | [`routing/link-carries-the-mount-prefix`](rules/routing.md#routing-link-carries-the-mount-prefix) |
| Routing | the query string is built by the same member that builds the path, and `url(...) . '?page=' . $n` is the concatenation the launderer exists to prevent | [`routing/a-leftover-link-key-is-a-query-string`](rules/routing.md#routing-a-leftover-link-key-is-a-query-string) |
| Routing | there is no base URL derived from `$_SERVER['HTTP_HOST']`; an absolute link comes from a configured origin or the call throws | [`routing/an-absolute-link-takes-a-configured-origin`](rules/routing.md#routing-an-absolute-link-takes-a-configured-origin) |
| Routing | a multi-tenant deployment configures one origin line with a capture in it rather than computing a base URL per request | [`routing/an-origin-is-per-mount-and-checked-at-boot`](rules/routing.md#routing-an-origin-is-per-mount-and-checked-at-boot) |
| Routing | there is no route cache to warm or to go stale — the scan is compile-time work keyed and invalidated with the compiled unit | [`routing/table-is-opt-in`](rules/routing.md#routing-table-is-opt-in) |
| Routing | there is no hand-written or annotation-scanned OpenAPI file to keep in sync — the document is a build output of the route table, and a program with no `#[Route]` produces none | [`routing/api-document-is-generated-from-the-route-table`](rules/routing.md#routing-api-document-is-generated-from-the-route-table) |
| Routing | no `/openapi.json` endpoint the running server assembles — the document is written at build time and served as a file, and there is no 3.0 or Swagger 2 output | [`routing/api-document-is-a-deterministic-build-artifact`](rules/routing.md#routing-api-document-is-a-deterministic-build-artifact) |
| Routing | a broken client contract is a failed build rather than a reviewer's judgement, and there is no suppression to wave one through | [`routing/api-diff-fails-a-breaking-change`](rules/routing.md#routing-api-diff-fails-a-breaking-change) |
| Routing | no convention routing — a class rename never moves a URL, because the derived path is inserted as source text once and is ordinary text from then on | [`routing/a-quick-fix-writes-a-derived-path`](rules/routing.md#routing-a-quick-fix-writes-a-derived-path) |
| Configuration | there is no INI dialect: the file is TOML, its name is `nvs.toml`, and no `php.ini` carries over under any syntax because the directive set shares almost no key with it | [`config/the-file-is-nvs-toml-and-it-is-toml`](rules/config.md#config-the-file-is-nvs-toml-and-it-is-toml) |
| Configuration | `memory_limit = 128M` becomes `memory = "128M"` — quoted, because the value is typed and the suffix is part of it — and `-1` for no limit becomes `false` | [`config/a-size-or-duration-is-a-quoted-string-with-its-suffix`](rules/config.md#config-a-size-or-duration-is-a-quoted-string-with-its-suffix) |
| Configuration | no comma-joined or `PATH`-joined strings: a list of roots is `["/a", "/b", "C:\\srv"]`, which is what makes a Windows absolute path spellable at all | [`config/lists-are-arrays-and-repeated-records-are-arrays-of-tables`](rules/config.md#config-lists-are-arrays-and-repeated-records-are-arrays-of-tables) |
| Configuration | `php.ini` silently takes the last of two copies of a key and ignores one it does not recognise; both refuse the boot here, naming the line | [`config/a-duplicate-key-is-an-error-and-so-is-an-unknown-one`](rules/config.md#config-a-duplicate-key-is-an-error-and-so-is-an-unknown-one) |
| Configuration | there is no `.user.ini` or `.htaccess` discovered beside the code — the file is read from one directory the operator chose, and it holds no source-tree state | [`config/nvs-toml-is-not-a-project-manifest`](rules/config.md#config-nvs-toml-is-not-a-project-manifest) |
| Configuration | there is no search path, no `PHPRC` and no compiled-in location: a `--config` list, else `./nvs.toml` in exactly the working directory, else the shipped defaults | [`config/the-root-is-config-else-nvs-toml-else-the-shipped-defaults`](rules/config.md#config-the-root-is-config-else-nvs-toml-else-the-shipped-defaults) |
| Configuration | a host without a `php.ini` runs on PHP's built-in defaults, which allow nearly everything; the shipped defaults here deny every capability and start in `production` | [`config/no-configuration-file-is-a-complete-configuration`](rules/config.md#config-no-configuration-file-is-a-complete-configuration) |
| Configuration | PHP's `--with-config-file-scan-dir` reads a directory in an order the build chose; here a `dir` include is every `*.toml` directly inside it, ascending by filename, written in the file itself | [`config/include-takes-a-path-or-a-dir`](rules/config.md#config-include-takes-a-path-or-a-dir) |

| Configuration | a relative path in `php.ini` resolves against whatever the process's working directory happens to be; here it resolves against the file that wrote it, so a config directory survives being copied whole | [`config/a-relative-path-resolves-against-the-file-it-is-written-in`](rules/config.md#config-a-relative-path-resolves-against-the-file-it-is-written-in) |
| Configuration | there is no `PHP_INI_SYSTEM` versus `PHP_INI_PERDIR` split between files: an included file clears the same ownership bar as the root file and may grant a capability, set `[limits.hard]` or add an `[[extension]]` | [`config/any-file-in-the-tree-may-set-any-directive`](rules/config.md#config-any-file-in-the-tree-may-set-any-directive) |

| Configuration | a credential arrives as a file — `password_file = "/run/secrets/db_password"` — with one trailing newline stripped and nothing else trimmed, rather than inline in the file or interpolated from the environment | [`config/a-secret-is-a-file-whose-content-is-the-value`](rules/config.md#config-a-secret-is-a-file-whose-content-is-the-value) |
| Configuration | nothing is re-read on the request path — no `.user.ini` scan, no per-directory override — and a reload that fails leaves the old configuration serving rather than half of each | [`config/the-config-is-an-immutable-snapshot`](rules/config.md#config-the-config-is-an-immutable-snapshot) |

| Configuration | `ini_set`, `ini_get`, `ini_restore` and `ini_get_all` are static members of `Core\Config`, a refused set answers `false` and moves nothing, and an accepted one is request-local | [`config/ini-set-is-core-config-set`](rules/config.md#config-ini-set-is-core-config-set) |

| Configuration | the same behaviour as `validate_timestamps`, chosen over the more forgiving keep-serving policy some caches adopt | [`config/a-broken-edit-fails-the-requests-that-resolve-it`](rules/config.md#config-a-broken-edit-fails-the-requests-that-resolve-it) |
| Configuration | a changed listen address is named in the reply rather than silently ignored until the next restart | [`config/a-reload-names-what-it-could-not-apply`](rules/config.md#config-a-reload-names-what-it-could-not-apply) |
| Configuration | there is no `SIGUSR2`, no `php-fpm reload` and no signal at all; the operator speaks HTTP to a local socket and gets a report back | [`config/one-local-control-socket`](rules/config.md#config-one-local-control-socket) |
| Configuration | `php --ini` names the files read and `phpinfo()` prints values from inside a request; here one offline command validates the whole tree in CI and names, per key, the file and line that set it and the one it overrode | [`config/check-and-dump-audit-the-tree-offline`](rules/config.md#config-check-and-dump-audit-the-tree-offline) |
| Configuration | there is no `php.ini-development`/`php.ini-production` pair to copy and no `APP_ENV`; staging is `production` with different configuration, not a third value | [`config/two-modes-and-the-default-is-production`](rules/config.md#config-two-modes-and-the-default-is-production) |
| Configuration | `APP_ENV` and its kind are ordinary `Core\Env::get` values with no effect on the runtime; the operator's switch is a reload of the root-owned file | [`config/no-environment-variable-selects-the-mode`](rules/config.md#config-no-environment-variable-selects-the-mode) |
| Configuration | "what does development mode change?" has a closed, printable answer, which no `APP_ENV` or `NODE_ENV` convention can give | [`config/a-mode-is-five-defaults`](rules/config.md#config-a-mode-is-five-defaults) |
| Configuration | a script can turn development defaults on for itself only where the operator opened a ceiling, and the flip never reaches another request | [`config/a-program-may-read-and-flip-its-mode`](rules/config.md#config-a-program-may-read-and-flip-its-mode) |
| Configuration | a per-directory `php.ini`, a `.user.ini` or a PHP-FPM pool keys on a directory the web server chose; an `[[app]]` block keys on the entry file's own path, so `nvs run` has the same identity as a served request | [`config/an-application-is-its-entry-file-path`](rules/config.md#config-an-application-is-its-entry-file-path) |
| Configuration | PHP applies the nearest `.user.ini` and stops; here a host-wide block and an application's own block compose, the narrower one winning only the keys it states | [`config/every-matching-app-block-applies-least-specific-first`](rules/config.md#config-every-matching-app-block-applies-least-specific-first) |
| Configuration | a per-directory `php.ini` can only move what `PHP_INI_PERDIR` allows; an `[[app]]` block sets any `[app.limits]` value up to `[limits.hard]` and grants a capability the global block withholds, so the root file denies and each application states what it needs | [`config/an-app-block-may-widen-bounded-by-the-global-ceiling`](rules/config.md#config-an-app-block-may-widen-bounded-by-the-global-ceiling) |
| Configuration | there is no crontab line and no scheduler API — a job, its cadence and its concurrency policy are an entry in `nvs.toml`, refused at boot when it cannot be armed | [`config/scheduled-work-is-a-config-block`](rules/config.md#config-scheduled-work-is-a-config-block) |
| Configuration | a seconds field or Quartz's `L`/`W`/`#`/`?` is refused at boot rather than accepted by whichever cron the host happens to run | [`config/cron-is-five-fields-and-nothing-more`](rules/config.md#config-cron-is-five-fields-and-nothing-more) |
| Configuration | the `flock`-and-hope guard a PHP deployment adds per cron job is one required word per entry, and forgetting it is a boot error rather than four copies of a nightly run | [`config/scope-has-no-default`](rules/config.md#config-scope-has-no-default) |
| Configuration | no `ini_set` or `.user.ini` can add, remove or retime a job — a request cannot touch the schedule at all | [`config/every-schedule-key-is-system`](rules/config.md#config-every-schedule-key-is-system) |
| Configuration | a cron-invoked `php` process gets no limits, no capability narrowing and no place to report but a mail spool; a scheduled run gets the deployment's `[limits]`, its `[capabilities]` and the escalation ladder because it is an ordinary isolate | [`config/a-scheduled-run-is-a-root-isolate`](rules/config.md#config-a-scheduled-run-is-a-root-isolate) |
| Configuration | there is no ambient timezone to fall back on and no anacron-style replay — the interval a host slept through is logged as skipped, not run late | [`config/a-missed-fire-is-skipped-and-a-dst-edge-fires-once`](rules/config.md#config-a-missed-fire-is-skipped-and-a-dst-edge-fires-once) |
| Configuration | a Redis on loopback needs one grant naming the store, not a host allow-list plus an exception for the loopback range the store lives in | [`config/cache-shared-is-the-grant-over-the-configured-store`](rules/config.md#config-cache-shared-is-the-grant-over-the-configured-store) |
| Configuration | `Redis::connect('/run/redis.sock')` and a socket path in a DSN a program builds are refused — the path has to be in root-owned configuration | [`config/a-unix-socket-is-admitted-only-where-an-operator-wrote-it`](rules/config.md#config-a-unix-socket-is-admitted-only-where-an-operator-wrote-it) |
| Configuration | `redis://`, `rediss://` and `unix:` are the only schemes `[cache.shared] url` reads — a credential is `[cache.shared] password` rather than userinfo, and a database index is `[cache.shared] database` rather than a path on the URL | [`config/unix-scheme-in-a-url-and-a-bare-path-in-a-host`](rules/config.md#config-unix-scheme-in-a-url-and-a-bare-path-in-a-host) |
| Configuration | `opcache.validate_timestamps` and `revalidate_freq` are `PHP_INI_ALL` in PHP; here no request may touch either, and there is no value that turns checking off | [`config/opcache-revalidation-is-system-class`](rules/config.md#config-opcache-revalidation-is-system-class) |
| Configuration | `opcache.file_cache` and `opcache.file_cache_dir` cannot be moved by `ini_set` or `.user.ini`; only the root-owned file sets them | [`config/opcache-file-cache-directives-are-system`](rules/config.md#config-opcache-file-cache-directives-are-system) |
| Packaging | opcache's file cache is keyed by path and revalidated by timestamp; an artifact here is keyed by the source's digest and the environment's, so a file built for another machine, compiler or extension set is never opened at all | [`packaging/an-artifact-is-one-immutable-content-addressed-file`](rules/packaging.md#packaging-an-artifact-is-one-immutable-content-addressed-file) |
| Packaging | opcache.file_cache_dir is taken as written; a directory that is world-writable or not owned by the runtime's own account refuses the process rather than the entry | [`packaging/the-checksum-proves-integrity-and-ownership-proves-trust`](rules/packaging.md#packaging-the-checksum-proves-integrity-and-ownership-proves-trust) |
| Packaging | OPcache revalidates the files it compiled; here adding a file that shadows an already-resolved name, or a module nothing references yet, invalidates the unit although no hashed file changed | [`packaging/autoload-probes-fold-into-the-cache-key`](rules/packaging.md#packaging-autoload-probes-fold-into-the-cache-key) |
| Packaging | there is no `.phar` and no archive format: the shipped file is the runtime itself with the source appended, and it is remade by its author rather than updated in place | [`packaging/nvs-build-compile-appends-the-program-to-a-copy-of-the-host`](rules/packaging.md#packaging-nvs-build-compile-appends-the-program-to-a-copy-of-the-host) |
| Packaging | a `.phar` can be stripped or compressed; a bundle's source is embedded byte for byte and is recoverable by anyone who looks | [`packaging/a-bundle-carries-source-not-artifacts`](rules/packaging.md#packaging-a-bundle-carries-source-not-artifacts) |
| Packaging | an `include` whose path is computed at run time has no filesystem to fall back on inside a bundle, so the build refuses it instead of the run failing on the user's machine | [`packaging/a-bundled-require-resolves-at-build-time`](rules/packaging.md#packaging-a-bundled-require-resolves-at-build-time) |
| Packaging | there is no `composer install` step inside the bundler: resolving dependencies and packaging them are two commands that compose, not one | [`packaging/build-compile-packages-what-is-on-disk-and-resolves-nothing`](rules/packaging.md#packaging-build-compile-packages-what-is-on-disk-and-resolves-nothing) |
| Packaging | `php` carries `-i`, `-a`, `-r`, `-f` and a lowercase `-v`; `nvs` inherits none of them, spells every operation as a subcommand, and declares exactly one short flag of its own | [`packaging/the-cli-surface-is-novis-own`](rules/packaging.md#packaging-the-cli-surface-is-novis-own) |
| Packaging | `php --help` lists flags the manual explains elsewhere; `nvs --help` is the explanation, and it names no repository document, no decision record and no file extension the binary does not act on | [`packaging/help-text-speaks-to-its-reader`](rules/packaging.md#packaging-help-text-speaks-to-its-reader) |

| Packaging | Composer lowercases and compares names case-insensitively; here a name is compared exactly so that one which resolves on one operating system resolves on all three | [`packaging/a-package-name-is-vendor-slash-name`](rules/packaging.md#packaging-a-package-name-is-vendor-slash-name) |
| Packaging | a Composer dependency is a name that resolves to whatever the registry serves today; here two archives with the same digest are the same package and two with different digests are different packages whatever they call themselves | [`packaging/a-package-is-its-digest`](rules/packaging.md#packaging-a-package-is-its-digest) |
| Packaging | composer.json drives the autoloader; here a populated `vendor/` resolves every name identically whether the manifest is present, absent or malformed | [`packaging/package-toml-is-a-tool-input`](rules/packaging.md#packaging-package-toml-is-a-tool-input) |
| Packaging | a Composer package may declare any PSR-4 prefix, including the application's; here a package file declaring `namespace App;` to reach the application's grants fails to compile | [`packaging/a-package-file-stays-under-its-declared-prefix`](rules/packaging.md#packaging-a-package-file-stays-under-its-declared-prefix) |

| Packaging | Composer's `scripts` (`post-install-cmd` and friends) and plugins execute at install time; here there is no hook, build step, macro or code generation of any kind | [`packaging/nothing-runs-before-the-program`](rules/packaging.md#packaging-nothing-runs-before-the-program) |
| Packaging | a Composer package's files may `require` anything the process can read; here a `..`, an absolute path or a symlink that leaves the package is a compile error | [`packaging/a-package-cannot-reach-its-host`](rules/packaging.md#packaging-a-package-cannot-reach-its-host) |

| Packaging | Packagist lets a publisher delete a release, which breaks every lockfile naming it; here the bytes stay fetchable forever and only selection refuses them | [`packaging/a-known-bad-version-is-retracted-not-deleted`](rules/packaging.md#packaging-a-known-bad-version-is-retracted-not-deleted) |

| Packaging | a call into an extension is checked by `nvs check` like a call into `Core`, not dispatched by name at runtime | [`packaging/extension-calls-are-statically-typed`](rules/packaging.md#packaging-extension-calls-are-statically-typed) |

| Migrating from PHP | the imported `.phpt` corpus passes at a structurally lower rate than a compatibility-first design would, and a failure in a listed class is intentional rather than a regression | [`php-migration/every-divergence-is-deliberate-and-listed`](rules/php-migration.md#php-migration-every-divergence-is-deliberate-and-listed) |
